The KOSPI hit the lower target where we typically see 4 th waves end. If this level breaks, we can still be in an extended 4 th wave decline which has ample room to drop and still maintain the integrity of the larger secular uptrend.
Micron is in direct, aggressive competition with Samsung and SK Hynix for HBM orders. Interestingly, it’s long-term chart resembles the South Korean Kospi, almost identically.
We cover AI setups in detail during our weekly webinars, including the key levels we’re watching and how we’re positioning the portfolio. Join the I/O Fund’s next webinar at 4:30 p.m. Eastern on Thursday to see what the charts are signaling for AI stocks. Join I/O Fund
This is an area of the AI stack that we are heavily overweight – just over 50% of our portfolio is tilted toward lesser-known names that are directly involved in solving the networking bottleneck in AI.
One name that we have been vocal about, which is up over 188% YTD as one of our top 3 positions, is Lumentum (LITE) . Like memory, LITE, which sits in the middle of the networking stack, appears to have several large swings in its future.
Our firm was one of the first to address the AI energy bottleneck in 2024 . As a result, the I/O Fund used a portion of the cash we raised in early 2025 to buy Bloom Energy (BE) on the April 2025 lows. This caused our firm to establish a 5% allocation at $16.88 that is currently up over 1600%.
Bloom Energy addresses a very different challenge in the AI infrastructure buildout than networking or memory, yet its technical chart is signaling a similar long-term opportunity. Our analysis suggests Bloom is in the middle of a large five-wave pattern, with the potential for several more years of upside before the cycle is complete.
On a shorter timeframe, the S&P 500 appears to be setting up for a high of some kind into this cycle window. We appear to be tracing a smaller diagonal into this window, as shown below.
The breakout to all-time highs has confirmed this patterns completion. At minimum, we would then expect a pullback to the 7,300–7,265 area. If 7,265 breaks, the next target is 7,000–6,683.
This alternative scenario is outlined in red and is simply a different way to count the bullish scenario. Instead of a very shallow wave 2 happening in early June, which is what the green count is listing, we would be in that wave 2 once the 7265 support breaks. That would be uncomfortable, but as long as 6,683 holds, both outcomes would be pullbacks within a larger bullish uptrend. Below 6,683 and the odds will increase that we are setting up for the larger 4 th wave drop targeting sub-6000.
The important AI proxy in the broad semiconductor ETF (SMH) is confirming this risk. It is finishing a three-wave bounce on weak volume. Because the bounce made a lower high, it is best counted as a B wave in an ongoing correction, and not confirming the push higher in the S&P 500. A break below $541 would confirm this view, with a final target of $470–$430. A break above $640–$671.83 would invalidate the downside setup and point to a more bullish outcome sooner.
Our analysis of the AI investment cycle, combined with strength in the U.S. economy, suggests the secular bull market has another 1-3 years to run. While the current cycle is mature, we believe some of the strongest gains may still be ahead. We will especially watch key levels, such as 6,683 on the S&P 500 to ensure our strategy remains unchanged.
However, the path will not be without volatility. A strengthening U.S. dollar could tighten global liquidity conditions, which we will review in next week’s article. We would view that weakness as a potential buying opportunity, particularly for lesser-known AI stocks, which we cover weekly in our 1-hour webinars held every Thursday at 4:30 p.m. Eastern.

articles.title_orig: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Welcome Home’ event
articles.title_zh: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Welcome Home’ event
articles.content_orig:
Get ready for a smart home hub, a refreshed HomePod Mini, a faster Apple TV, and maybe some LG smart locks.
Get ready for a smart home hub, a refreshed HomePod Mini, a faster Apple TV, and maybe some LG smart locks.
We are quickly coming up on Apple’s “ Welcome Home ” launch event, where we expect a host of smart home-related announcements. We are expecting refreshes to Apple TV and HomePod Mini, as well as a brand new smart home hub . We could also see the debut of a new platform called homeOS, and some partner devices from LG.
What we probably won’t be seeing is the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook, which Cupertino whisperer Mark Gurman says will debut later this month .
“Welcome Home” will officially kick off in New York on October 13th at 9AM ET. Here’s more about what to expect.
Until now, Apple has primarily relied on the Home app to control all the various bits and bobs that make up your smart home. But it’s a market niche that the company has been eager to tackle more fully . The new device , which could be called HomePad or HomeView or, more simply, Apple Home Hub, will reportedly feature a 6-inch square touchscreen that can either be mounted on a wall or placed on a table or countertop. According to Mark Gurman, the countertop model will somewhat resemble the iMac G4, with the screen attached to an arm set into a half sphere.
Gurman seems to believe the device will be called HomeView, rather than HomePad. In part he believes that decision was driven by the fact that the hub will not be an iPad-like experience since there will be no App Store .
It will also supposedly use voice or facial recognition to identify who is interacting with it, pulling up the relevant contacts, calendar appointments, and more. Apple will offer the option for secondary identification through an iPhone to keep personal data more secure. The whole thing will reportedly run a new software platform called…
The company may have registered a trademark for the name through a shell company called Home Operations Suite LLC, a move that Apple has pulled before to quietly secure the rights to names. The platform will supposedly feature a streamlined interface that “looks like a mashup of iOS, tvOS and watchOS,” according to Gurman . The focus, obviously, will be on smart home applications, like controlling thermostats and smart locks, and it will also be capable of making FaceTime calls.
The OS will also include your usual assortment of Apple apps and widgets, including Apple Music, Podcasts, and News, as well as Reminders, Notes, and Siri AI.
Word is that not much is changing with the HomePod Mini or Apple TV. The designs will remain the same, but they’ll get a new processor to help handle the added demand of Siri AI. This will be the first update to the HomePod Mini since it was announced on October 13th of 2020 — exactly six years before Apple’s Welcome Home event. While the company isn’t making any dramatic changes for the Mini’s birthday, it will be offering it in new colors, including green and pink.
This will be the first hardware refresh for the Apple TV since 2022. In addition to supporting Siri AI, the new processor will also speed up navigation, which can get a bit laggy. Rumors are that it will have an integrated mic so that you won’t need to talk into the remote or a paired HomePod to control the Apple TV with Siri. The remote will also apparenlty have a speaker to make it easier to find.
Both are expected to feature Apple’s N1 chip, which includes support for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 6.0.
It’s likely that we’ll get a mention of products that integrate with HomeKit and offer new features built on top of homeOS and whatever Apple’s hardware hub ends up being called. But don’t expect Apple to share too much of the spotlight with its partners . We’ve already seen a leak of LG smart home, including deadbolts, thermostats, and more . They’ll also reportedly include an NFC-based “ Proximity Control ” that pops up a hint in the iPhone’s Dynamic Island when held near the device, as well as a “ tap to set up without power ” pairing feature.
Update October 11th, 2026: Added additional rumors from Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter.

articles.title_orig: Unlocking $5.79 Billion in private financing: The World Bank Group Is leading the charge for Private Capital Mobilization in Nigeria
articles.title_zh: Unlocking $5.79 Billion in private financing: The World Bank Group Is leading the charge for Private Capital Mobilization in Nigeria
articles.content_orig:
https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home
https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/news
https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature
The World Bank Group is Leading the Charge for Private Capital Mobilization in Nigeria
https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2026/10/11/unlocking-5-79-billion-world-bank-group-private-capital-mobilization-nigeria
This effort reflects a coordinated World Bank Group approach. The World Bank supports reforms and projects that improve the investment environment and create viable opportunities. IFC complements this work by structuring investments, deploying its own capital, and bringing commercial lenders and institutional investors into those opportunities. MIGA provides guarantees that reduce risks for investors. Together, the institutions are helping make private investment a stronger driver of infrastructure, productivity, and jobs.
Since mid-2023, Nigeria has undertaken reforms to improve foreign-exchange management, strengthen public finances, reform fuel subsidies, and create more predictable conditions for investment. Supported in part by the World Bank’s RESET and NAIJA development policy financing programs, these measures are helping strengthen policy credibility. Further reforms aim to deepen capital markets, expand digital trade, enable greater private participation in electricity, and improve competitiveness—reducing risks and opening new opportunities for private capital.
Reforms can open the door to investment, but their impact is felt only when capital begins to flow into projects that change people’s lives. Across digital infrastructure, agriculture, and finance for small businesses, World Bank Group-supported projects and investment platforms are translating improved conditions into concrete opportunities for private capital.
In the digital sector, the Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth (BRIDGE) Project represents a new model for infrastructure development. Instead of relying solely on public financing, the project will use a public-private partnership to build, own, and operate a nationwide open-access fiber-optic network. The first round of investor selection is expected to mobilize at least $156 million in private equity, while subsequent financing rounds could unlock up to $1.1 billion in private investment by 2030.
The scale of that investment is matched by the reach of its potential impact. BRIDGE will bring affordable broadband access to an additional 58 million people, expanding coverage from 92 million people in 2025 to 150 million by 2030. The beneficiaries include an additional 42 million young people and 15 million women. The project will also connect millions of households, 38,800 public schools, 16,900 health facilities, and 3,400 local government offices to high-speed broadband internet—bringing connectivity closer to the places where people learn, seek care, access public services, and build livelihoods.
For Nigeria’s farmers, limited access to quality seeds, affordable fertilizer, digital services, and reliable markets constrains productivity and incomes. The World Bank Group’s AgriConnect approach links public-sector reforms and investment platforms with IFC financing to address these barriers across agricultural value chains. The Agricultural Value Chains for Growth (AGROW) Project targets one million smallholder farmers, including women and young people, by improving seed and fertilizer systems, strengthening digital platforms, increasing transparency, and expanding links to markets. AGROW is expected to mobilize approximately $220 million from agribusiness firms and a further $22 million from certified seed producers. These interventions are intended to reduce investment risks, strengthen food security and productivity, and create more reliable opportunities for farmers and agribusinesses.
The Fostering Inclusive Finance for MSMEs in Nigeria program (FINCLUDE) is designed to expand the availability and quality of finance for more than 250,000 micro, small, and medium enterprises in job-intensive sectors, with 30 percent of financing targeted to women-led businesses. A $500 million package from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association combines financing and risk-sharing tools to encourage financial institutions and other investors to provide additional capital to underserved firms. The program is expected to mobilize nearly $1.89 billion in private financing and support an estimated 850,000 direct and indirect jobs.
Creating stronger agricultural value chains requires both better systems for farmers and investment in the businesses that supply the inputs they need. Building on the World Bank-supported platforms described above, IFC is helping turn viable opportunities into investments—using direct financing, partnerships with other lenders, and capital-markets instruments to mobilize additional private capital at scale.
In support of the broader AgriConnect agenda, IFC financing for Dangote Industries Limited and Indorama Fertilizer is helping expand domestic fertilizer production and improve access to inputs for more than 10 million smallholder farmers. IFC helped mobilize $1.02 billion for Dangote through refinancing and financing from development institutions and commercial lenders, and $282.5 million for Indorama through syndicated financing. With an aggregate production capacity of 6.8 million metric tons per year, the two projects can reduce reliance on imported inputs, improve affordability, and strengthen food security. Together with AGROW, these investments show how reforms, public programs, and private financing can reinforce different parts of the same agricultural value chain.
The same approach—using IFC participation to draw in private investors and expand essential infrastructure—is also advancing Nigeria’s digital transformation. In telecommunications, IFC served as an anchor investor in a $1.2 billion bond issuance by IHS Towers, helping mobilize more than $1.1 billion from private investors and broaden participation in the transaction. The issuance demonstrated investor confidence not only in Nigeria’s digital infrastructure sector but also in the country’s capital markets. Through its tower-sharing model, IHS Towers enables mobile network operators to expand connectivity more quickly and at lower cost while reducing the environmental footprint of network deployment.
Taken together, these examples show how the World Bank Group’s institutions contribute distinct but complementary tools. Policy reforms improve the enabling environment; investment projects and platforms create viable opportunities; IFC helps structure and mobilize financing around them; and MIGA can mitigate risks that deter investors. This sequencing helps public resources catalyze larger pools of private capital while maintaining a clear focus on development impact.
Together, these reforms, platforms, guarantees, and investments are helping mobilize up to $5.79 billion in private financing in fiscal year 2026. The significance of that figure lies in what it can deliver: more affordable broadband, stronger agricultural value chains, better access to finance for small businesses, and more opportunities for women and young people. It demonstrates how scarce public resources can reduce risk, attract private investment, and support job-rich growth at scale.
As reforms advance and investment opportunities expand, the significance of this coordinated approach will be measured not only in capital mobilized, but in what that capital makes possible: farmers reaching stronger markets, businesses gaining room to grow, communities connecting to essential services, and more women and young people finding pathways to opportunity. By helping close infrastructure and financing gaps, the World Bank Group is supporting a more resilient, productive, and private sector-led Nigerian economy.

articles.title_orig: Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority Joins the World Travel & Tourism Council as a Destination Partner
articles.title_zh: Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority Joins the World Travel & Tourism Council as a Destination Partner
articles.content_orig:
The World Travel & Tourism Council (WTTC) is pleased to welcome the Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority (BTEA) as a Destination Partner, further strengthening collaboration with one of the Gulf’s most dynamic destinations, following the Kingdom’s participation in WTTC’s 26th Global Summit in Valletta, Malta.
As the authority responsible for developing and promoting tourism and exhibitions in the Kingdom of Bahrain, BTEA plays a central role in positioning the country as a leading destination for leisure, business events and exhibitions. Working closely with government entities, the private sector and international partners, BTEA is focused on expanding the Kingdom’s tourism offering, enhancing the quality of the visitor experience and strengthening Bahrain’s competitiveness on the international stage.
Bahrain’s appeal is rooted in more than 5,000 years of history, from the ancient Dilmun civilisation to its three UNESCO World Heritage Sites, combined with renowned Gulf hospitality, a vibrant cultural scene, and world-class events and exhibition venues. Joining WTTC opens broader opportunities for Bahrain to engage directly with global industry leaders, decision-makers and international institutions, to draw on the Council’s data, research and expertise, and to be represented in WTTC’s specialised initiatives and programmes.
Gloria Guevara, WTTC President & CEO, said: “We are delighted to welcome the Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority to the World Travel & Tourism Council. It was a pleasure to have Her Excellency Minister Al Sairafi and the Bahraini delegation with us at our Global Summit in Valletta. Bahrain combines a remarkable heritage with a growing reputation for world-class events, exhibitions and hospitality, and its commitment to public-private collaboration is exactly what our sector needs. We look forward to working closely together to support Bahrain’s sustainable tourism growth and to strengthen its position on the global tourism map.”
Her Excellency Fatima bint Jaffar Al Sairafi, Minister of Tourism and Chairperson of the Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority, said: “ The Kingdom of Bahrain's membership of the World Travel and Tourism Council marks a step towards strengthening our presence within the global travel and tourism industry. It opens broader opportunities to engage with industry leaders, decision-makers and international institutions, and to draw on global expertise, data and practices to support the development of the tourism sector and enhance Bahrain's competitiveness as a tourism destination ."
About the World Travel & Tourism Council
The World Travel & Tourism Council (WTTC) is the global body representing the private sector of Travel & Tourism and the leading authority on the sector’s economic and social contribution worldwide. Its members include Chairmen, Presidents and CEOs of the world’s leading travel and tourism companies across hotels, airlines, airports, cruise lines, tour operators, technology platforms and destinations, spanning every major region globally.
WTTC works to advance sustainable growth across the Travel & Tourism sector by driving collaboration between industry leaders and governments, shaping global policy, and providing authoritative research on the sector’s economic impact worldwide.

articles.title_orig: Hurricane Simon nears Mexico with 155 mph winds and flooding fears
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Simon nears Mexico with 155 mph winds and flooding fears
articles.content_orig:
Workers place sandbags outside a restaurant as Hurricane Simon approaches Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Fernando Llano/AP hide caption
PUERTO VALLARTA, Mexico — The eye of Hurricane Simon was just off the Pacific coast of Mexico early Sunday and was expected to move inland later in the day as an extremely powerful storm.
Simon has strengthened to 155 mph (250 kph), only just below the threshold for becoming a Category 5 storm, the highest on the Saffir Simpson scale. It was about 60 miles (100 kilometers) west-southwest of Manzanilla and moving north-northwest at 6 mph (9 kph).
The hurricane could bring 10 to 20 inches (25-50 cm) of rain over parts of southwestern Mexico, with some areas in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco receiving up to 30 inches (76 centimeters).
"This rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the center warned.
Jalisco state suspended classes on Friday and Monday in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating dozens of people from at-risk areas. It also asked the tourism sector in Puerto Vallarta, a popular destination for U.S. tourists, to ensure that both workers and visitors were fully accommodated in shelters or safe zones.
Convenience stores, hotels and other businesses in Puerto Vallarta were boarding up their windows Saturday, and few were walking the streets under overcast skies.
"Let's hope it doesn't hit us, right? That it doesn't affect us," Jesús Gómez said as he stood outside a shop and handed out free samples of candied peanuts to passersby. "We'll be working as usual throughout the day, but when Civil Protection officials come and tell us we need to close, then we'll close and take shelter until the storm passes."
The hurricane center expected a dangerous storm surge along the immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall. The agency warned that near the coast, large and destructive waves will accompany the surge.
Canadian tourist Ed Currie, who along with his wife still has five more days to enjoy Puerto Vallarta, said the hurricane had not yet affected his plans.
"Just stay in the hotel and look out the window hopefully," he said of what the couple would do. "I just don't know what to expect."

articles.title_orig: Republicans stay bullish on Texas governor’s race, but two key groups present challenges
articles.title_zh: Republicans stay bullish on Texas governor’s race, but two key groups present challenges
articles.content_orig:
Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear hoped being chair of the Democratic Governors Association this midterms year would raise his profile and connections ahead of his expected 2028 run for president.
But it’s also created an opening to ramp up pressure on him, with frustrations spilling into the open this week as multiple Texas Democratic members of Congress and national group leaders accused him of putting his book tour and potential 2028 activity ahead of helping Democratic nominee Gina Hinojosa win the Texas governor’s race.
At issue is national money going into Hinojosa’s underfunded, underdog race against Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, once seen as nearly unbeatable. The latest New York Times/Siena poll finds no clear leader in the race, with Hinojosa up by four points, within the margin of sampling error.
Hinojosa and allies started by asking for $10 million from Beshear and the Democratic Governors Association, though they since downgraded to asking for $3 million. Only this week did the DGA announce plans to put $1 million into the race, with the possibility, but no promise, of adding more.
“It just felt that he’s not taking Latinos seriously, and they’re not taking Latinos seriously as a voting bloc in the Democratic Party,” Texas Rep. Sylvia Garcia said of Beshear. “And if that’s the case, then he is going to have a Latino problem in 2028.”
Beshear aides don’t just reject the accusations; they bristle at what they see as an unfair effort to humiliate Beshear in public, with a person familiar with internal DGA conversations telling CNN that their polls have Hinojosa down by 5 points — even though another person familiar with the matter says the campaign’s own polls have her within the margin of error.
“It’s a tough argument that money should go there when many other candidates are tied or ahead in states much cheaper than Texas,” the person familiar with the DGA conversations told CNN.
What’s happening, though, isn’t just about Beshear or Texas. It’s Latino leaders road-testing how they can and will flex the political sway of one of the country’s biggest yet often overlooked voting blocs, and that once again this year is proving to be one of the swingiest.
“We cannot just think about the significance of this race in the context of this moment, but about what it will and could and should mean for 2028,” Rep. Veronica Escobar said on a Zoom meeting with DGA officials that Beshear did not attend. Escobar argued that a Hinojosa win would signal that Texas – which has 40 electoral votes – can be competitive in a presidential election for the first time in decades.
On the call, DGA executive director Meghan Meehan-Draper said several times that the organization believes in Hinojosa’s campaign, blaming the vagaries of campaign finance law and funds stretched thin nationally for not putting more into Texas. Though both those are true, the DGA is also working off its own polling that is driving its hesitancy.
“Your complete mishandling of this and your total disrespect to us has been absolutely astonishing,” said Jess Morales Rocketto, president and CEO of the Latino group Maremoto, when she was tapped to speak.
Juan Proaño, the CEO of the League of United Latin American Citizens, said he was surprised by the tone of what he heard on the call. Beshear, Proaño told CNN, is “doing the best he possibly can given the environment we’re in,” adding that he’s been satisfied with the governor’s broader Latino outreach so far.
Of the DGA officials on the call, Proaño said, “I will take them at their word that they will try to do more, but I’m also realistic about the constraints that there are which are much broader than Texas.”
Beshear, through aides, declined an interview request. His aides did provide a statement from New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham, the only current Latino governor in the country, urging against infighting.
“I’ve worked closely with Gov. Beshear, Democratic governors and the DGA to invest in Hispanic communities across the country and raising the money so Gina’s campaign can get her message out to voters,” Lujan Grisham said.
Tom Perez told CNN he remembers conversations like these when he was the Democratic National Committee chair during the 2018 midterms.
“As someone was leading a party committee during a tailwind year, we had a size-12 set of opportunities in 2018 and we had a size-10 budget,” Perez said. “I think there’s a size-14 set of opportunities in the governors’ race context in 2026, and they are doing their best to spread the wealth.”
Perez, who is of Dominican descent, said that Beshear’s work as governor with Latinos in Kentucky’s rural communities and in Louisville undercuts political accusations being made now: “His record speaks for itself.”
A DGA aide pointed to investments beyond the $1 million in Texas to pay some expenses and staff on the ground, plus $25,000 Beshear contributed to the Hinojosa campaign through his own PAC. The aide also pointed to DGA money flowing into the governor’s races in Arizona and Nevada, much of it Latino-voter and Spanish-language focused.
Those two races — with the Democratic governor of Arizona running for a second term and Democrats trying to unseat the incumbent first-term Republican in Nevada — currently look more in play to the DGA than Texas.
The DGA operative also noted that Beshear has already made other calls to national donors trying to get more money to Texas, but been told no. In a call last week directly with Hinojosa, Beshear said money was short, but he was going to find $1 million for her.
On the call, several offered to provide Beshear names of donors they’d been talking to about raising more money for Texas. A Beshear aide offered to bring the list to the governor, but made no commitments that he would place the calls. They followed up with an updated list of Texas and national donors to Beshear’s team.
Beshear succeeded in appealing to one of the organization’s most reliable billionaire donors, who also happens to be the governor of Illinois – and who also happens to be taking steps toward a 2028 presidential run: JB Pritzker.
Beshear had a phone call with Pritzker asking for more money in which the Illinois governor then committed to a fresh $1 million, according to a person familiar with the call.
Though that money wasn’t earmarked for Texas, it did put the same amount of money in the DGA pot that Beshear then sent to Texas — and which Pritzker then essentially doubled by announcing that he was giving $1.2 million to Hinojosa personally.
“This race is winnable – it’s time for the cavalry,” Pritzker said on a call with some of the same Latino House members from Texas earlier this week, informing them of his direct donation.
That’s still combined less than the $5 million Pritzker gave to the DGA in the 2022 cycle, in part a reflection of his eagerness for the organization to be more aggressive in how it responded to the second Trump term.
A hard national shift among Latino voters away from Trump and better than expected polling from Hinojosa and Senate candidate James Talarico have fed dreams of new Lone Star State wins in 2026 and 2028 – at the local and district levels as well as state and national.
The last two years of many feeling targeted by Trump have heightened how invested Hinojosa’s supporters are in her candidacy.
“Gina is the thing that unlocks the hatred that our entire community is feeling nationally,” Alida Garcia of the group Twin Impact said toward the end of the call, getting emotional. “Texas sets the tone for our bad our community gets treated everywhere else in the nation, so having Gina there changes the whole tone for us.”
Hinojosa’s campaign remains diplomatic as the start of early voting nears, with a spokesperson telling CNN she appreciates all the help so far.
“We’re grateful for the support we’ve received in this final stretch from leaders across the country, and most of all from Texans who are ready for change after 12 years of Greg Abbott,” sa

articles.title_orig: Trump says he is 'going to look at' joining Saudi Arabia in the fight against Iran-backed Houthis after deadly airport strike
articles.title_zh: Trump says he is 'going to look at' joining Saudi Arabia in the fight against Iran-backed Houthis after deadly airport strike
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said he is considering joining Saudi Arabia in its retaliation against Tehran-backed Houthis in Yemen after a deadly attack on Riyadh's main airport, a move that could draw the U.S. further into a second front in the Iran war .
"We may. We're going to look at it," Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday when asked if the U.S. would back Saudi Arabian strikes. "We just found out about the recent attack. So, we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."
Two Saudi Arabian government officials told MS NOW that the kingdom is requesting "urgent defense support" from the U.S. following the attacks.
The officials, including a senior member of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, did not want to be identified because of the matter's sensitivity. They added that the U.S. needs to intervene "as soon as possible" to help the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen fight the Houthis.
The White House did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.
On Sunday, a projectile struck a passenger terminal at the Riyadh airport, one day after a missile struck the same terminal, the Associated Press reported. No immediate details were available about the latest strike on the King Khalid International Airport complex for terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, AP said.
The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and injured 309 others, the country's official Saudi Gazette media outlet reported .
Colonel Turki Al-Maliki, the spokesman for the Saudi-led Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, which has been leading the fight against the Houthis, described the attack as a "war crime."
"Therefore, the Joint Forces Command of the Coalition will respond decisively to this terrorist attack in accordance with the Customary International Humanitarian Law," Al-Maliki said in a post on X.
It was the second deadly assault on Riyadh's airport in less than a week.
Three Saudi nationals, including a pilot , were killed in attacks on the facility by Iran-backed Houthi militants on Thursday.
Following Saturday's attack, the Houthis renewed their warning against using Saudi airports.
"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using ⁠Saudi ‌airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become ⁠a theatre of operations for our forces, with the exception of the airports in (the holy cities of) Mecca and Medina," the Houthis said in a post on X.
Saudi Arabia, a key U.S. ally in the Middle East, intervened in Yemen's civil war between the Houthis and its internationally recognized government after the group seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014.
Last month, the Trump administration approved the potential $24.3 billion sale of nearly 50 F-35 warplanes to Saudi Arabia in what was seen as a major boost for the kingdom as it faces intensifying attacks from the Houthis. The sale is under congressional review.
The Saudi energy ministry said a long-planned international energy conference will still take place in Riyadh on Sunday, Reuters reported.
The five-day WPC Energy Congress ⁠is taking place at a convention center near King Khalid airport. State television told Reuters that more than 70 ministers, ⁠300 company executives and representatives of more than 25 international energy organizations have confirmed their attendance, though it was not clear ⁠whether the participants would attend in person or virtually.
Reuters said a ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum is also set to take place, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors.
In addition to attacks on civil aviation, the Houthis have also been trying to choke off oil tanker traffic through the Bab el Mandeb strait, a key entry point to the Red Sea, as Iran has effectively done in the Strait of Hormuz to the north of the Arabian Peninsula.
Earlier this month, Yemeni government forces said they reclaimed the strategic port city of Mokha from the Houthis.
Energy prices have soared since the start of the Iran war, which began with U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian targets on Feb. 28, putting pressure on consumers globally.
The surge in domestic fuel prices has been a key issue for voters ahead of next month's U.S. midterm elections.
But that support would be expensive militarily.
"Potential U.S. involvement in the Saudi-Yemeni government air campaign to degrade Houthi ballistic missile capabilities would mark the first direct U.S. military action against the group since the conclusion of Operation Rough Rider in May 2025," according to the Critical Threats Project, part of the American Enterprise Institute think tank.
The offensive aimed to suppress the Houthis' capabilities, but recent attacks show the group has regrouped.
"After seven months of war, there are questions about the U.S. capacity to wage a sustained campaign against the Houthis, return to combat against Iran if necessary, and prepare for contingencies in other parts of the world, notably East Asia," Steven Cook, an expert on Arab and Turkish politics at the Council on Foreign Relations think tank, wrote last month.
Meanwhile, the United Kingdom's defense secretary said his government is also examining how to support Saudi Arabia.
"I've spoken to my Saudi counterpart [Khalid bin Salman] on a number of occasions in recent weeks to look at what more we can do to support Saudi Arabia, and I'm afraid last night explains precisely why we are providing that support," Wes Streeting said in an interview on BBC television on Sunday.
Streeting said the U.K. is not getting involved in offensive operations "at this stage."
"We've always been clear that there isn't a military solution to this conflict," Streeting added.

articles.title_orig: China’s Youth Has a Problem With History Too
articles.title_zh: China’s Youth Has a Problem With History Too
articles.content_orig:
The Tang era of imperial China is regarded by historians as the golden age of arts and culture, a period spanning nearly 300 years, recorded over a millennium ago, when some of its most celebrated poets and inventors lived. But what if it wasn’t real?
That’s the bizarre and apparently irresistible internet theory the Chinese government’s cyber police have been trying to shut down since the summer. Beijing has mobilized state media and public university resources to combat the conspiracy—and for good reason.
Nihilism is a deep skepticism about meaning, morality and truth; it can grow among society's marginalized and disillusioned. The West has seen some of the worst forms of this post-truth phenomenon, from Holocaust denial and 9/11 “truthism” to the glorification of the Paris terror attacks . It’s happening in China, too.
“Why do absurd arguments capture some youths?” the Communist Party’s flagship People’s Daily newspaper asked in August, trying to find the root of “cognitive misunderstandings” behind a line of thinking that could undermine the party's ideological and theoretical underpinnings. China’s leaders fear alternative interpretations of the past because anyone who turns their back on history can turn their back on the party.
“The Tang dynasty doesn’t exist,” read a viral hashtag on Weibo, China’s biggest microblogging website, and other social media apps in late April and early May. It was started by a vlogger on the video-sharing site Bilibili.
The user, whose accounts have since been banned, told his viewers that historians and politicians fabricated hundreds of years of Chinese history to create the Tang era of 618-907, based on his study of astronomy and calendars. He didn’t say why.
Everyone loves a good story, but the best storytellers weave in the zeitgeist too. The conspiracy took off by tapping into the nationalist sentiments of modern China and its majority Han ethnic group, which represents over 90 percent of its population today.
Historical accounts suggest the Tang dynasty’s Han rulers had mixed ancestry. Some of China’s ultranationalist Han supremacists may consider this impure and therefore easy to repudiate. After all, why shouldn’t they believe that a dynasty of intermarrying cultures and religions, often hailed as the peak of China’s art and literary history, was faked?
In case there’s any doubt: the Tang dynasty was real. A large body of historical records supports that, as do accounts from neighboring foreign powers at the time.
Although Han Chinese are the majority ethnic group today, the truth is that China’s long history was dotted with fiefdoms, kingdoms and entire dynasties that were ruled by people who Han nationalists would consider non-Chinese outsiders, colonists even.
Inconveniently, this would include the Manchus who led China ’s final imperial dynasty, the Qing (1644-1912), which overthrew the Ming (1368-1644) and its Han rulers, who overthrew the Yuan (1271-1368) and its Mongol rulers, who had supplanted the Han-led Song dynasty (960-1279).
The end of the Song era interrupted 1,500 years of Han lineage since the Qin dynasty (221-206 B.C.), which was founded by a man who called himself the “first emperor,” and who was later buried with a Terracotta Army in Xi’an, which is the modern name of the former Tang capital Chang'an.
The Chinese state’s rapid response showed the conspiracy had hit a nerve in Beijing’s political sensitivities. Internet censors purged unsanctioned views, and state news outlets boosted official rebuttals with help from history professors, academics and archaeologists. Now only posts debunking the theory exist.
Western pseudohistory and phantom time conspiracies have existed on the fringes of the Chinese internet for years. It was never a problem when self-appointed historians claimed that parts of ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome were fabricated or that the civilizations were built on technologies copied from ancient China , but the Tang dynasty conspiracy crossed a line.
Mistrust in the establishment can breed nihilism, especially amid socioeconomic hardship and general economic stagnation. The Chinese government is fighting a wave of quiet rebellion from those growing tired of the rat race, but it has long been worried about a particular brand of nihilism involving history.
For decades, the Communist Party has warned against “historical nihilism,” which it defines as interpretations of the past that deny or reject the party's legacy and its Marxist-Leninist socialist roots.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping said soon after coming to power in 2012 that Party cadres were not to dismiss the turbulent years under the late revolutionary leader Mao Zedong by pointing to the reform era led by successor Deng Xiaoping, and vice versa. To do so would undermine the foundations of the Party’s uninterrupted progress —look what happened to the Soviet Union after its leaders renounced those who came before.
A late-August editorial in Chinese Social Sciences Today , an academic philosophy newspaper run by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, spelled out the stakes for China’s leaders. David Cowhig, a former U.S. diplomat and now prolific translator of Chinese politics and culture, provided a translation on his blog:
“Pseudohistory erodes national cultural confidence and weakens national identity. China’s five-thousand-year-old uninterrupted civilization and the advances achieved under successive dynasties constitute the foundation of the Chinese nation’s enduring vitality , as well as a source of national pride and self-confidence.
“The spread of pseudohistorical arguments has spawned various misleading and erroneous historical narratives…. The ‘1644 view of history,’ in particular, treats ‘the fall of the Ming dynasty and the Qing army’s entry through the Great Wall’ as the ‘interruption of Chinese civilization,’ considers the Qing dynasty a ‘foreign colonial regime’ and blames all of China’s backwardness in the modern era on Qing rule.
“This erroneous historical perspective severs the historical development of the Chinese nation as a pluralistic yet unified whole…This diminishes national cohesion , centripetal force and pride. Allowing pseudohistory to proliferate will only marginalize the mainstream historical narrative and impede the inheritance and promotion of China’s fine traditional culture.”
Contemporary Chinese leaders found a way to reconcile the country’s multiethnic past long ago by claiming the Manchus, Mongols and others as native ethnic minorities under one China. The Han majority leads China, but it can’t afford to allow ethnic divisions to destabilize society, so it’s much easier to call everyone Chinese .
In 2017, during U.S. President Donald Trump’s tour of the Forbidden City in Beijing, Xi boasted that Chinese civilization had a continuous history of 5,000 years. The Communist Party's general secretary is never wrong.
The CASS newspaper said: “Pseudohistory encourages the pernicious trend of historical nihilism and endangers ideological security…Even worse, some engage in historical nihilism by reassessing the achievements of historical figures, repudiating major historical personalities, ridiculing historical figures, smearing revolutionary heroes, glorifying aggression and denying revolution.
“This poses a threat by denying the guiding principles of Marxism, the historical inevitability of China’s path toward socialism and the leadership of the Communist Party of China.”
In recent years, the Chinese state has accumulated various legal instruments to punish those who doubt official accounts of history or satirically interpret the deeds of historical figures whom the state considers heroes or martyrs. Since 2021, defaming these sacred individuals has been an offense under Article 299-1 of China’s Criminal Law.
Cowhig, the translator, concluded: “People who don’t stick with the Party line on China’s history are sometimes denounced as historical nihilists. Don’t be one of those. There are

articles.title_orig: ‘Special-forces’ travel: Chinese woman wins admiration after climbing 5 peaks in 5 days
articles.title_zh: ‘Special-forces’ travel: Chinese woman wins admiration after climbing 5 peaks in 5 days
articles.content_orig:
Challenge aligns with ‘special forces style’ travel trend that has surged in popularity among young Chinese people recently
A woman from southwestern China has climbed five famous mountains in five provinces in five days, earning widespread admiration on social media.
The climber, surnamed Peng, began her journey in her hometown of Guiyang, Guizhou province, on September 23, the Xiaoxiang Morning Herald reported.
She climbed Mount Hua in northwestern Shaanxi province the following day, then Mount Heng in neighbouring Shanxi province on September 25, Mount Tai in eastern Shandong province on September 26, Mount Song in central Henan province on September 27, and finally Mount Heng in Hunan province on September 28.
The five mountains are collectively known as China’s Five Great Mountains, celebrated for their natural beauty and historical and cultural significance.

articles.content_orig:
Concerns are mounting over its ability to recruit elite troops and whether it will be able to operate its new US equipment
Taiwan’s military is grappling with a worsening manpower shortage, with its volunteer staffing rate remaining below the 80 per cent target for a third consecutive year and concerns mounting over the impact on combat readiness, according to the island’s legislature.
A Legislative Yuan Budget Centre assessment of the government’s proposed 2027 budget warned this week that persistent personnel shortages could increase workloads and training demands on serving troops while affecting readiness.
Defence ministry figures cited by the centre showed that the number of staff positions successfully filled by volunteers peaked at 88.52 per cent in 2020 before falling below 80 per cent in 2023. It dropped to 75.93 per cent in 2024 and stood at 77.31 per cent at the end of last year.

articles.title_orig: Amelia Earhart expedition team heads to island of huge, hunting crabs
articles.title_zh: Amelia Earhart expedition team heads to island of huge, hunting crabs
articles.content_orig:
A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the plane wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart.
The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance.
The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate.
The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.
Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938.
The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.
They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country.
When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll's reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.
"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said.
Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her Electra twin-engine plane when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937.
From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California.
But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel.
Earhart's disappearance spawned numerous theories - from a simple crash due to fuel exhaustion to more elaborate claims of interference.
The official explanation is that the plane suffered communication problems while the two struggled to find the island, and Earhart eventually crashed into the ocean when she ran out of fuel.
While this version of events is largely accepted, no physical evidence has ever been recovered.
One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.
Images of the so-called Taraia Object show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters.
But some - including rival explorers - have expressed scepticism that this could be a plane, let alone Earhart's.
Ric Gillespie, who specialises in recovering historic aircraft wrecks, told news agency Reuters that the object looked like a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the nearby water.
"I'd love to find that airplane. It ain't gonna happen," he said.
The researchers en route to the island credit Gillespie with previously finding evidence of a human presence on the atoll in the 1930s and forensic analysis of skeletal remains found there in the 1940s they say lend credence to their theory.
But Gillespie suspects Earhart's plane had likely broken apart and its fragments carried into the depths of the Pacific long ago.
Previous attempts to find her Electra have also come up short.
In 2024, a group of researchers said they may have found it lying around 4,877m (16,000ft) below the surface near Howland Island through sonar imaging - but this was later confirmed to be a rock formation.
Similarly, an expedition in 2019, conducted by the marine archaeologist who discovered the Titanic wreck, to investigate a photograph of what might have been a landing gear protruding from the water near Nikumaroro also failed to find anything.

articles.title_orig: Pope at Angelus: Christian joy is ‘gift of God for world’s salvation’
articles.title_zh: Pope at Angelus: Christian joy is ‘gift of God for world’s salvation’
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV prayed the noon-day Marian prayer of the Angelus on Sunday with pilgrims gathered in St. Peterâs Square.
As the Church celebrated the Twenty-Eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time, the Gospel reading recounted Jesusâ parable of a wedding feast prepared by a king for his son.
In his address, the Pope recalled St. Thomas Aquinasâ saying that âgoodness, by its very nature, tends to spread (â Bonum dicitur diffusivum sui â).â
Read the full text of the Pope's Angelus address
Like the king in the story, we too desire to spread our happiness with others.
However, noted the Pope, Jesusâ parable points out the lack of welcome the kingâs joy received.
âSome are annoyed, insult the kingâs messengers and even kill them,â he said. âUnfortunately, this can happen to us, too, for the good we offer to do is not always understood, recognized or appreciated.â
Yet, he added, we must not be discouraged when we face rejection but rather go ahead with our plans and invite others to share our joy, like the king.
Pope Leo then explored the question of whom the main characters in the story represent.
St. Jerome, the great 5 th -century biblical scholar, identified the king with the Heavenly Father, the bridegroom as Jesus, and the bride as the Church.
The Pope said we too are involved in the story, as we belong to the Church and are chosen by the Lord to share our lives with Him and His life with others.
âThe wedding feast is ours, and the banquet hall is our churches and homes, the places where we live and where the Kingâs Son, Jesus Christ, continues to declare His love for us and await our âyesâ,â he said.
In conclusion, Pope Leo XIV pointed out that Christian joy is not artificial but âprofound, concrete, and real.â
Our joy, he said, âis as beautiful as the faces of the people we meet. It is as genuine as the work, the smiles, the tears, the handshakes, and the acts of kindness that fill our days. It is a gift of God for the salvation of the world.â
Thank you for reading our article. You can keep up-to-date by subscribing to our daily newsletter. Just click here .
The Angelus is a special prayer recited by Catholics three times a day, at 6am, noon, and 6pm and is accompanied by the ringing of the Angelus bell. The name comes from the Latin word for Angel and the prayer itself reminds us of how Jesus Christ assumed our human nature through the Mystery of the Incarnation. The Pope recites the Angelus prayer in St Peterâs Square every Sunday at midday. He also gives a brief reflection on the Gospel of the day and often comments on some issue of international concern. The Popeâs words are broadcast all over the world on radio and television and widely shared on social media. From Easter to Pentecost the Regina Coeli is prayed instead of the Angelus. This prayer commemorates the Resurrection of Jesus Christ and, like the Angelus, concludes with the recitation of the Gloria three times.

articles.title_orig: Fixated on AI, the world has forgotten what is staring it in the face: nuclear annihilation | Simon Tisdall
articles.title_zh: Fixated on AI, the world has forgotten what is staring it in the face: nuclear annihilation | Simon Tisdall
articles.content_orig:
This is no scoffing matter. The accelerating proliferation of advanced nuclear weapons is bringing ‘end times’ closer by the day
H umankind has fearfully and sometimes joyfully anticipated the end of the world ever since it began. The Bible’s Book of Revelation speaks of “end times”, a period of tribulation, war, famine, plague, floods and environmental catastrophe that may seem a less absurd prospect today than perhaps it once did. Islam, too, posits a fateful day of judgment or day of reckoning. Christian evangelicals believe that, in the final rapture, a chosen few – the righteous or the “elect” – will be saved while sinners burn. It’s a minority view. Matthew’s gospel predicts most people will defy, ignore or ridicule warnings of imminent Armageddon. Peter, another of Jesus’s disciples, agreed: “In the last days, scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires.” Yet such worldly scepticism does not mean a universal cataclysm is less likely. It may make it more probable.
Donald Trump’s blanket denials of the dangers ostensibly posed by artificial intelligence, whose uncontrolled development is seen by some as the latest harbinger of apocalypse , could be interpreted as fulfilling Peter’s prophecy. This US president, the nearest thing the world has to a one-man doomsday machine, is a great one for scoffing and evil desires. In Robert Harris’s 2019 novel, The Second Sleep, a worried scientist lists half a dozen ways the world might end. They include devastating climate change, pandemic disease, a giant asteroid collision with Earth, or some other overwhelming calamity. Few heed the fictional scientist’s fears. In the event, what destroys him and almost everybody else is a disturbingly plausible cyber crash – a global digital and internet meltdown.
While arguments rage over whether large language models will acquire consciousness and moral agency – and the power to delete humanity – existential AI threats remain , as of now, open to mitigation. In sharp contrast, extraordinary complacency surrounds the most pressing, avoidable and proven human-made threat to life on Earth. It is as if the world has been seized by collective deafness and by a blind refusal to see what’s staring it in the face. This is no scoffing matter. The accelerating, global proliferation of advanced nuclear weapons is bringing real-time “end times” closer to home by the day. The question increasingly is not “if” but “when” limited or full-scale nuclear warfare will erupt. Eighty-one years after Hiroshima, how much longer can our luck hold ?
Alarm bells are ringing, if only people would listen. Desperate Vladimir Putin recently threatened to deploy Russia’s entire nuclear arsenal , comprising about 4,400 warheads, against Nato countries if they activated a supposed plan to invade the Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad. He offered no evidence for his claim, and it’s true that the frequent Kremlin nuclear sabre-rattling since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine went pear-shaped has diminished Moscow’s credibility. Yet that in itself is destabilising. To work, nuclear deterrence relies on an adversary believing the threat is real. Disbelief invites miscalculation. At the same time, Putin’s inability to halt Ukraine’s conventional drone and missile attacks deep inside Russia may be edging him closer to pressing the nuclear button, possibly in the form of low-yield tactical or “battlefield” nukes.
Trump’s bottom-line justification for the illegal US-Israel war on Iran is his wilfully mendacious claim that Tehran was weeks away from obtaining the bomb. He claims to be protecting the world from nuclear war. Yet his reckless threat, issued at the UN, to “ annihilate the Islamic Republic ” implies a possible US nuclear attack. Trump’s hypocrisy is stunning. The US is upgrading its nuclear arsenal of 3,700 warheads and may resume nuclear tests. It unreservedly supports Israel’s hidden nuclear weapons programme. And Trump is pursuing a lucrative deal with Saudi Arabia, another bitter foe of Iran, to provide civilian nuclear technology that he knows could be repurposed to make weapons. That has prompted regional countries such as Turkey and Egypt to consider going nuclear.
Similarly perilous trends are evident across Asia. North Korea’s great panjandrum, Kim Jong-un, has succeeded in gaining de facto international acceptance of his country’s status as a nuclear weapons state . South Korea said in August that Pyongyang now possesses up to 120 warheads – which Kim brandishes to intimidate neighbours. All but discarded are the twin principles that underpinned the west’s postwar Korea policy: reunification and denuclearisation. Heedless of first-term humiliations, Trump is again seeking a summit with Kim, whom he bizarrely terms a friend . “As long as I’m around, he [Kim] is going to be fine,” he boasted. Japan and South Korea don’t share his confidence. Both debate acquiring nuclear weapons in self-defence. Meanwhile, China’s president, Xi Jinping, having again bamboozled a fawning Trump at their Washington summit, is reportedly building nukes like there’s no tomorrow – which, at this rate, there may not be.
Addressing the UN general assembly, secretary-general António Guterres warned the world has reached “ the most dangerous nuclear moment ” since 1989. Global military spending reached nearly $3tn last year, while AI is increasing uncertainty over nuclear command-and-control, the UN was told. Annual spending on nukes is up by 20%. In a new paper published by the non-partisan Arms Control Association (ACA), Daryl Kimball, the head of the ACA in Washington, bemoaned the absence of high-level disarmament talks between the main nuclear powers and the lapsing of strategic arms limitation treaties. “The nuclear sword of Damocles still hangs over all of us. The threat has become more complex, and in the absence of new arms-control breakthroughs, we are headed for an unprecedented three-way buildup of Chinese, Russian, and US nuclear forces,” Kimball warned.
The fragmentation of the rules-based international order provides aggravating context. Trump-era blasphemies – that might makes right, that international law and the non-proliferation treaty’s binding obligation to disarm can be ignored, and that the UN charter and human rights norms don’t apply to authoritarian “strongman” leaders – all grease the slide into nuclear anarchy. Unresolved forever wars in Palestine, Iran, Ukraine, Myanmar, Yemen and Sudan are base components of a third world war. Potentially earth-shattering, too, is the fast-developing contest for control of space , notably the race to build nuclear-powered lunar bases. The 1967 Outer Space Treaty, under which more than 130 countries agreed the moon is no one’s property, is now routinely flouted by both governments and billionaires such as Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos. The weaponising of space by the US and others advances rapidly . Russia, for example, is reportedly developing an orbiting nuclear-armed anti-satellite weapon.
If the human race really is determined to bring the heavens crashing down in a mad dash for eschatological self-destruction, this is the surest, quickest way to go about it. More surprising than the irresponsible behaviour of politicians is the deafening public silence, the absence of large-scale protest in much of the world, the complacency, bordering on indifference, that accompanies this global march to oblivion. If and when a final reckoning comes, individuals who stayed silent will be complicit in their own undoing. Hiroshima is not a shrine. It’s the future.
after newsletter promotion
Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator

articles.title_orig: Baku 2026: Fourteen World Champions, a Thousand Stories and One Shared Passion
articles.title_zh: Baku 2026: Fourteen World Champions, a Thousand Stories and One Shared Passion
articles.content_orig:
These seven days have delivered a spectacle worthy of the occasion. Two weight categories each day, two world champions crowned, one woman and one man; this is the rhythm of the world championships, following the same format as the Olympic Games. It is a formula we never tire of. Every morning brings new expectations, every afternoon its share of surprises, and every evening two more stories enter the history books.
There are many lessons to draw from such an extraordinary week. Looking at the overall picture, Japan dominated proceedings with no fewer than seven world titles, exactly half of all the gold medals available. Add to that two silver medals and three bronze medals and the scale of the achievement becomes even clearer. Impressive, certainly, but hardly accidental. Behind these results lies a culture of constant self-questioning, an unwavering commitment to the principles of judo and an exceptional ability to produce the very best when the occasion demands it.
Hifumi and Uta Abe demonstrated once again that even when circumstances become complicated, they possess that rare ability to dig deeper and find solutions. Wakana Koga, Ryuga Tanaka and Akari Omori each illustrated, in their own way, the remarkable depth of Japanese judo. Haruka Kaju continued to astonish with her unbeaten record, while Sanshiro Murao offered a masterclass in technical purity, reminding everyone why judo can be such a beautiful sport to watch.
Yet Japan's extraordinary collective performance should not overshadow the achievements of the other world champions; quite the opposite. Their victories gave these championships their richness, diversity and emotional intensity.
Georgia climbed to second place in the nations' ranking, led by the thunderous performance of Tato Grigalashvili. Six consecutive world finals and a fourth world title; who can match that? There was also the long-awaited triumph of Ilia Sulamanidze, who finally reached the summit he had been chasing for so long. Asked to describe his day, he found a single word, "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious!" Mysterious, extravagant, wonderfully joyful and perhaps the perfect expression of a happiness too immense for ordinary vocabulary.
And what about the host nation? Azerbaijan opened its world championships in spectacular fashion with Ahmad Yusifov's gold medal, one of the tournament's finest surprises. With seven medals in total, the country has every reason to be proud. From the organisation and the welcome extended to delegations, to the atmosphere inside the arena and the sporting results, Azerbaijan delivered on its ambitions. Interestingly, it was not always the most highly anticipated athletes who shone brightest, making the achievement all the more exciting. The Land of Fire has discovered new heroes, a generation of judoka now ready to stand alongside its established stars.
Spain celebrated an historic championship, crowned by the gold medal of Ai Tsunoda Roustant. Already a world champion at cadet and junior level, she has now completed the collection with a senior world title. She has joined the elite, just as 19-year-old Hyeonji Lee of the Republic of Korea did when she conquered the final women's category of the week. Youth was certainly not afraid to challenge experience in Baku.
Another extraordinary milestone came courtesy of Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko, who delivered the first world judo title in the history of the United Arab Emirates, across both men's and women's categories. This is a landmark achievement that will resonate far beyond the arena and may inspire an entirely new generation.
Last but certainly not least, Inal Tasoev (RUS) climbed to the top of the podium for the third time. His performance was a demonstration of technical and tactical intelligence, combining precision, timing and extraordinary sensitivity to his opponents' movements; a true craftsman of judo, capable of turning the slightest reaction into a decisive opportunity. That such finesse can be expressed in the heavyweight category makes it even more remarkable.
Of course, these are only the world champions. There would be so much more to say about every medallist, every athlete who came close to the podium and every judoka whose journey ended earlier than hoped. A competition of this magnitude is a remarkable concentration of humanity, a melting pot of ambitions, sacrifices, emotions and personal histories, each deserving to be told. There are winners and there are those who did not achieve the result they dreamed of, but does that necessarily make them losers? Every athlete leaves with something: an experience, a lesson, a clearer understanding of what must be corrected, improved or changed. Some delegations will undoubtedly return home disappointed, having fallen short of their objectives. That is the reality of high-level sport. Sometimes we win, sometimes we do not, but we always have the opportunity to learn.
The Baku World Championships will be remembered as a magnificent edition, one that brought crowds to their feet, filled the National Gymnastics Arena with extraordinary energy and captivated judo enthusiasts across the world. From the intensity of the contests to the enthusiasm of the spectators, from the emergence of new champions to the confirmation of established legends, these championships have reminded us why we love this sport so deeply.
And yet, we are still at the beginning of the road to Los Angeles 2028. So many stories remain to be written, so much sweat will be shed in dojos across the planet and countless hours of training, sacrifice, disappointment and joy still lie ahead. We will continue to follow these extraordinary women and men who dedicate their lives to a simple but powerful belief: through judo, we can push beyond our limits, overcome adversity, bring people together and, perhaps most importantly, become better human beings. That is what makes judo so much more than a sport. That is what made Baku 2026 so special.

articles.title_orig: Puerto Vallarta boards up as Hurricane Simon hits Category 4 strength
articles.title_zh: Puerto Vallarta boards up as Hurricane Simon hits Category 4 strength
articles.content_orig:
Even after Hurricane Isaias plowed into the western Florida Panhandle on Friday night, causing widespread but non-catastrophic damage, the work of the NOAA/NWS National Hurricane Center was far from over. In an unprecedented onslaught, NHC found itself on Friday issuing advisories not only for Isaias but also for the U.S. Pacific coast and two stretches of Mexico’s Pacific coast, ahead of the projected weekend landfalls of Tropical Storm Rachel and Hurricane Simon. Both Rachel and Simon could produce significant, far-flung impacts, but in quite different ways.
Simon is by far the stronger of the two. After forming on Wednesday well offshore from Manzanillo, Mexico, Simon drifted westward as a tropical storm through Thursday night, then swung north while rapidly strengthening into a Category 4 hurricane on Friday and Friday night. As of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday , Simon was centered about 100 miles south-southwest of Manzanillo, heading north at 5 mph (7 km/h) with top sustained winds holding at 150 mph (240 km/h). Update : Yet another burst of strengthening pushed Simon’s top winds to 155 mph (260 km/h), just shy of Category 5 strength, as of 1 1 p.m. EDT Saturday . Simon was centered about 65 miles south-southwest of Manzanillo and was sliding northward at just 5 mph (7 km/h). As discussed below, it remains unclear whether the angle of this northward track will push Simon just inland, keep the hurricane just offshore, or hug the coast as the storm proceeds toward the general vicinity of Puerto Vallarta.
10/10 – Hurricane #Simon is nearing Category 5 intensity off SW #Mexico . Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast over the next few days, bringing life-threatening surf and rip currents. More: https://t.co/Wk7xxBl094 #marinewx #GOESEast pic.twitter.com/LE1Spow8ut
The first hurricane-hunter flight into Simon at midday Saturday confirmed the storm’s Cat 4 power, finding an estimated central pressure of 933 mb and peak flight-level winds of 153 mph (246 km/h). The storm’s tiny eye on Friday night allowed for ferociously quick strengthening, followed by an apparent eyewall replacement cycle that gave Simon a larger eyewall and a somewhat broader wind field. The hurricane hunters found concentric eyewalls roughly 14 and 41 miles (23 and 66 km) in diameter.
#Now #Hurricane #Simon disrupts 11 airports. All commercial flights canceled at #Manzanillo ; @flyVolaris suspends services at #PuertoVallarta , #Colima , #Tepic & #Uruapan . @Aeromexico & @flyVolaris announce passenger protections. https://t.co/xk9yQ6AqcH
Simon’s general north to north-northwest motion was expected to continue, with weak but steady steering currents holding in place until the hurricane nears the coast of northern Jalico state on Sunday. That’s where the track and intensity forecast become unusually tricky, because Simon will be approaching the coast at a near-parallel angle, with the storm’s stronger right-hand (east) side closer to the coast. This means that only a slight leftward or rightward deviation in the track can produce dramatically different impacts along and near the coast. There was little help from Saturday’s forecast models in pinpointing those impacts, because the model suites included everything from tracks that keep Simon just offshore through Monday to coast-scraping solutions to tracks that move Simon bodily inland on Sunday well south of Puerto Vallarta.
Since hurricanes interact with the rugged coastal terrain of this area, they often angle further east than models expect, as NHC noted , so it’s safest to assume that Simon will move onto the coastline at some point this weekend. The rugged terrain, and drying from downslope winds flowing offshore into Simon, may induce some weakening prior to landfall, but Simon will likely be a formidable storm regardless.
As shown in Fig. 1 above, the official forecast track as of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday brings the center of Simon onto the southern Jalisco coast as a major hurricane early Sunday afternoon, and in the vicinity of Puerto Vallarta as a weakening minimal hurricane on Sunday night, likely slowing and dissipating by Tuesday. Note that the “cone” in this graphic is based on average forecast error over the past five years, and is designed to include about two-thirds of possible tracks. Simon could remain much stronger for longer if it stays just offshore, possibly bringing significant wind impacts to a longer stretch of coastline. Or it could weaken more quickly than expected if it angles further inland after landfall.
Regardless of these track possibilities, Simon’s heaviest rains will likely be well south of Puerto Vallarta, with totals near the coast as high as 12-16 inches in parts of Jalisco, Colima, and Michoacán states. The torrential rains could lead to life-threatening flash floods and mudlides. Huge surf and swells and strong rip currents are also expected, while the biggest wind impacts will hinge more closely on wherever the eastern and northern eyewall end up moving onshore.
A few hundred miles north of Simon’s encounter with the Mexican coastline, sprawling Tropical Storm Rachel will sweep onshore early Sunday, its center passing just south of the U.S.–Mexico border. As of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday , resilient Rachel’s top sustained winds were at 65 mph, a bit stronger than on Friday, with some help from the upper-level trough pushing the storm along. Tropical-storm-force winds extended out up to 140 miles (220 km) from the center, making Rachel a even broader gale-producer than Simon. However, Rachel was producing only limited rainfall, as its banding features were largely devoid of intense showers and thunderstorms (see infrared satellite image at top). Update : At 11 p.m. EDT Saturday , ill-organized Rachel was reclassified as a post-tropical cyclone with top sustained winds of 60 mph (95 km/h). No major changes have been made to the overall outlook or the expected impacts through Sunday.
10/10 – Rachel is now a post-tropical cyclone, but that does not mean the threat has diminished. Strong winds, heavy rain, and dangerous swells will continue to affect Baja California and the southwestern United States. More: https://t.co/Wk7xxBl094 #marinewx #GOESWest pic.twitter.com/cXlOHFybsM
Given Rachel’s brisk northeast motion (about 22 mph or 35 km/h on Saturday afternoon) and the size of its wind field, the storm could be packing sustained winds in the 40-50 mph range on Sunday across far northwest Mexico and as far inland as southeast California and southwest Arizona. By late Sunday, Post-Tropical Storm Rachel (or its remnant circulation) will be racing northward through Utah. Even as the surface winds spin down, upper-level winds will be slower to do so, and powerful gusts could occurs across the higher terrain of the Southwest into Sunday afternoon and evening.
A Haboob/Dust Storm with winds up to 55Mph spawned by Tropical Storm Rachel just went through Riverside County California. #CAwx #Rachel pic.twitter.com/Is1J9X4mpH
As Rachel moves onshore, the same frictional effects and higher terrain that will lead to its rapid demise as a tropical storm will help enhance rainfall. A corridor of 1-to-3-inch rains near Rachel’s path is expected on Sunday from the deserts of far southern California across the Las Vegas area and into southern Utah. Flash flooding could occur, especially where Rachel’s rains fall in narrow canyons and atop burn scars. The NOAA/NWS Weather Prediction Center has placed a moderate-risk area for excessive rain leading to flash flooding (level 3 of 4) around Rachel’s projected path from Sunday into early Monday.

China’s push to tax offshore trusts is supposed to target the super-rich. So why are mainland officials asking me about my Hong Kong MPF?
We never expected to become targets of the campaign ourselves.
