articles.title_orig: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is already beating the foldable iPhone in a way I can’t ignore
articles.title_zh: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is already beating the foldable iPhone in a way I can’t ignore
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
When I first got my hands on the iPhone Duo , I admittedly dismissed the unfolding animation that would soon become a highlight of online discourse. I was less interested in the smooth transition as content shifted from one screen to another and more focused on details such as the matte inner display and seemingly invisible crease.
But in the weeks since Apple unveiled its first foldable iPhone, which drops Oct. 23 , I’ve seen countless examples on social media of people trying to recreate that buzzed-about animation on their Android foldables. While the Play Store offers plenty of launchers for customizing Android phones — including ones that mimic the iPhone’s home screen — this appears to be one iOS design element that users are particularly eager to bring to their devices.
Sometimes, you really can’t predict what people will care about most — or the lengths they’ll go to imitate a feature.
The primary phone people have used to recreate the iPhone Duo’s cascading transition effect is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 , which debuted in July with a passport-size foldable design ahead of Apple’s release . Unlike iOS, Samsung’s One UI interface, which runs on top of Android on Galaxy devices, doesn’t include a folding animation. Instead, content simply transitions from the Z Fold 8’s cover screen to its inner display once the phone is opened about halfway. I never considered this a deficiency until I saw the flood of positive reactions to the iPhone Duo’s fluid transition effect.
To bridge that gap, several creators have posted videos explaining how to use third-party apps and developer tools on GitHub to get a similar effect on the Z Fold 8, with caveats like “ the smoothness and quality won’t be the same ‘” and “ install it [at] your own risk .” (That’s encouraging!) The steps don’t seem particularly complicated, and some options appear to have cropped up in the Play Store as well.
I’ve chosen to forgo installing these Duo-copycat apps on my precious Galaxy Z Fold 8 for two reasons. First, I’m not much of a risk-taker. Second, I’m not interested in imitating an aesthetic element of Apple’s software with a derivative version, especially when the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a standout foldable device in its own right. While the value of the Duo’s sleek animation has since grown on me, I’m not quite desperate enough to retrofit it onto a foldable phone that’s just as functional without that flourish.
Don’t get me wrong: I think Apple’s combination of hardware and software expertise will elevate the iPhone Duo in a way that merits the attention the phone has received, despite being relatively “late” to the foldables game . But I also think it’s more tasteful for consumers to embrace what each phone-maker does best, rather than shoehorning in a competitor’s feature for something as superficial as an animation effect.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is one of my favorite phones I’ve tested this year, earning it a CNET Editors’ Choice Award. Its versatile design is optimized for both vertical and horizontal content : I can stream YouTube videos and movies on the 7.6-inch inner display, then rotate it to seamlessly scroll through social posts. The crease is barely noticeable, and the battery easily lasts all day. The 5.5-inch cover screen never feels cramped, while its sharp corners give the phone a highly polished look. And despite lacking a telephoto lens, the Z Fold 8’s dual rear cameras pull their weight, capturing crisp, vibrant photos.
The iPhone Duo shares many attributes with the Z Fold 8, including a palm-size design, 7.6-inch inner display and dual rear cameras. Those similarities prompted Samsung to post a series of salty tweets after Apple debuted its foldable last month, including one that reads , “Let us know when you’re done reheating our leftovers.”
That said, I am curious how app developers might optimize their platforms for the iPhone Duo in ways we haven’t seen with other foldable phones. While the Android operating system spans a wide range of devices and configurations, iOS developers only have to cater to a single foldable, potentially leading to a more tailored and streamlined experience. We got a glimpse of how Netflix is building its app for the Duo, and it’ll be interesting to see how both Apple and other third-party developers take full advantage of the phone’s 1.4:1 aspect ratio in ways that could make its predecessors seem behind the curve in that regard.
“Borrowing” features from each other is what phone-makers do best. Down the road, it’s possible companies such as Samsung will implement foldable capabilities that Apple rolled out first, and vice versa. Heck, Apple’s delayed entry into this space means it had time to analyze what worked well for its competitors before jumping in with its own rendition. It’s just how the industry works.
So maybe the Galaxy Z Fold 9 — or whatever Samsung decides to call the follow-up to the Z Fold 8 — will have its own nifty opening animation. But until Samsung itself embraces the idea, I’ll stick with using the standout foldable as-is.

articles.title_orig: Exclusive | At Davos, Kimberly Guilfoyle Boasted of Private Jet Trips, Luxury Stays
articles.title_zh: Exclusive | At Davos, Kimberly Guilfoyle Boasted of Private Jet Trips, Luxury Stays
articles.content_orig:
Eric Deters says US ambassador to Greece asked him to pay off American Express credit card bill in return for access
A Trump donor accused Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece and Trump family ally, of engaging in a “quid pro quo” by asking him to pay off her $100,000 debt in exchange for access to administration officials.
Eric Deters, a former congressional candidate and lawyer, told MS Now on Thursday that Guilfoyle had “ambushed” him last year with an offer to provide access to government officials if he paid her American Express credit card bill, before her US Senate confirmation hearing as ambassador to Greece.
“It absolutely was a quid pro quo,” Deters told the network in response to a Wall Street Journal report that she had pushed him for the money.
“Kimberly Guilfoyle is a grifter,” he added.
The Guardian has asked Guilfoyle’s lawyer for comment.
Jesse Binnall, a lawyer for Guilfoyle, told the Wall Street Journal that Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of the messages, but that she was “owed a balance” for travel and speaking at events before her nomination. Deters told the Journal that he did not owe Guilfoyle any balance.
The report is the latest allegation about Guilfoyle’s conduct as a US official. Deters shared messages he and Guilfoyle exchanged in which the US ambassador to Greece promised him “ride or die” access to Trump administration officials if he wired American Express $100,000.
Asked about the report during a press conference in Athens on Wednesday, Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, said he would not address the allegations. He reaffirmed his support for the US embassy in Greece adding, “ Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here.” Asked again about the reports on Thursday, Rubio refused to comment.
The top Democrats on the House foreign affairs and Senate foreign relations committees have asked Rubio to open an investigation into Guilfoyle’s conduct as an ambassador.
A spokesperson for the Democratic staff of the Senate foreign relations committee confirmed to the Guardian that they were requesting further information and continuing to investigate.
JD Vance similarly expressed hesitation, similar to Rubio, on Thursday when asked to respond to a US ambassador offering access to government officials in exchange for money to pay off debts.
“With that hypothetical, Jen, obviously I don’t love that,” the vice-president replied. “But I don’t know exactly who you’re talking about. I don’t know the full details. What I find with these stories is you never want to comment in a purely abstract way because a lot of times the details really matter,” he added.
Concerns about Guilfoyle’s conduct were first raised in September when the Wall Street Journal reported she had used her position to invite Greek lobbyists to sit in on official diplomatic meetings and promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company.
Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the ranking Democrat on the Senate foreign relations committee, sent a letter to Rubio on Tuesday , asking him to look into the allegations against Guilfoyle.
“Such actions do not serve US credibility overseas and risk undermining US diplomacy,” Shaheen wrote. “In advance of your upcoming travel to Greece , I request an immediate review of Ambassador Guilfoyle’s actions and a clarification of what steps have and will be taken to avoid undue influence and even the appearance of a conflict of interest.”
Separately, Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House foreign affairs committee, sent a letter to Rubio in September, requesting more information about Guilfoyle’s conduct, her relationship with the Greek construction and energy company and her relationship with the lobbyist.
“If these reports are accurate, Ambassador Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position,” Meeks wrote.
Guilfoyle, 57, was once a member of the Trump family’s inner circle, having been engaged to Donald Trump Jr, the US president’s eldest son, for roughly three years. The couple ended their engagement in 2024, and shortly after taking office, Donald Trump nominated Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece.
But now further allegations accuse Guilfoyle of promising a Trump donor, Eric Deters, access to the Trump administration in exchange for a $100,000 payment to American Express.
Deters shared messages exchanged between himself and Guilfoyle with the Wall Street Journal in which she reportedly pleaded: “Honey please I need you to get this done for me today.”
Deters said Guilfoyle had promised him thatshe would “be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever” if he made the American Express balance. Deters said he never made the payment.
In other messages, Guilfoyle reportedly raised concerns about her communications with Deters becoming public and reprimanded him for not being discreet. “Eric, I really wish you would stop papering all these things. It’s really dangerous and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on Signal,” she is said to have written in one message.
“What a nightmare, you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing,” Guilfoyle reportedly wrote in another message.
A lawyer for Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of messages Deters shared with the Wall Street Journal.
It is unclear whether Shaheen or Meeks will ask Rubio for further information about the latest report. The Guardian has asked Meeks and Shaheen for comment.

articles.title_orig: The 2026 CFMOTO SR-S750: Riding China's attempt at a Japanese sportsbike
articles.title_zh: The 2026 CFMOTO SR-S750: Riding China's attempt at a Japanese sportsbike
articles.content_orig:
I was set to hate it. I felt I had to. It was made in China, and while I think CFMoto, on general principles, makes pretty good bikes, what business does it have attempting an in-line four? That engine configuration is the stuff of legend. The Chinese want to splash in that pond, they wanna bring their A-game.
The SR-S was indeed an in-line four, and I’d sharpened my fangs on in-line fours back when they breathed fire, hailed Satan, and tank-slapped their way to red-line.
I kept riding in-line fours after the Japanese engineered the tank-slapping out of them, and their unique shriek will always be one of the great songs of my people. Nothing assaults your ears and screams “Fast” like an in-line four being hammered through the gears.
It all began in 1969 with the Honda CB750-Four, the bike that started the so-called superbike era. The prototype was unveiled in 1968 at the Tokyo Motor Show, and the first production bikes arrived in the USA the following year. Kawasaki upped the ante when it unveiled its 900cc Z1 in 1972…and away we all went.
In-line fours got bigger, went a hell of a lot faster, and schooled several generations of riders in sheer terror, while simultaneously addicting them to industrial doses of adrenaline. And jail.
Around the turn of the century, it was decided that 1000cc was kinda the right capacity for an in-line four superbike, and while Suzuki flirted with a 1400cc in-line four from 2011 to 2008, that fat bastard was never a contender for the superbike crown. Suzuki was alright about that. It also produced what many still believe to be the finest in-line four ever made – the K5-engined GSX-R1000 – which was itself the obvious performance progression of the just-as-legendary GSX-R750, the bike that defined “handling” 25 years ago. Suzuki figured it would just jam its 1000cc monster engine into that wickedly agile 750cc bastard to see if it danced.
It did. But to many people, the GSX-R750 still danced just that little bit better. The 1000 went harder, but the 750 handled sharper. That was the argument. And the argument was ultimately settled by the market. Suzuki stopped making the GSX-R750 in 2016, but it was essentially the same bike it had made in 2011. The GSX-R750 was still being sold in the USA up until 2019, but that was just unsold 2016 stock.
The in-line 1000 had won out. Size mattered, it seemed.
But ask anyone who has ever ridden the GSX-R750 and the GSX-R1000 which one handled better, and they will tell you it was the 750. It was always the 750.
We now live in a world where in-line fours are all 1000cc track monsters, and the market all seems to be about parallel twins – the sensible cardigan of the motorcycle world.
Older riders, who once sold important organs to buy in-line fours, are now too old and too scared to even care what 14,000rpm in top means on an in-line four. Younger riders are far too risk-averse and have been bludgeoned by legislation and the policing that goes with it to even think about red-lining an in-line four in all six gears.
So why the Hell would CFMoto produce an all-new four-cylinder in-line 750? It was going great guns with its parallel twin offerings. They were incredible bang-for-your buck, improving with each model run, and absolutely making the big Japanese Four sit up and pay attention.
Why this four-cylinder winged thing, with its strange rear wheel, and cutting-edge suite of electronic whizz-bangery?
No idea, and I could care less. Maybe the Chinese are just throwing this 750 SR-S out there to see what would happen. Maybe they wanted to make the Japanese crazy. Maybe it was a little of both.
Utkarsh was very kind when he first wrote about this bike, but then Utkarsh is young, full of hope, open of mind and burdened with a sweet disposition. I am not, and I was determined to hate it.
And then I saw it in the flesh and thought: that’s not too bad, actually. Sure, the rear wheel looks like it’s meant to slice giant potatoes, but close inspection revealed those munted inserts could be removed with an Allen key and thrown into the sea.
The rest of it looked cool. Very cool. But I was certain it was not going to be a GSX-R750 when I rode it. And I was right. It was not. It was a very long way away from Suzuki’s epic sportsbike statement.
CFMoto’s SR-S is a very different statement. Sure, you hit the starter button and it instantly fires into that intoxicating angry beehive hum only an in-line four can make. I remember looking at it after I started it up and muttering: “Well, you certainly sound like you mean business…”
And it did, but it was a different kind of business. It was a business for our time. A gentler, friendlier, easier-to-ride kinda business, because we live in just such a world – or we’d like to. Or the government would like us to. So the SR-S is not the GSX-R.
For starters, there is no racer’s crouch happening here. You sit canted forward, but not in a way that puts all your weight on your arms and forces your neck back. Think sports-tourer rather than sportsbike.
It seemed to handle well, but it was shod with Maxxis SP tyres, and I could not bring myself to see how they dealt with me at Max Stupid. I’m funny about tyres. Most people are. There are brands you like and trust and there are brands you don’t. I have had nothing to do with Maxxis. I read good things about them, but the Internet is full of lies.
Ridden at a few degrees less than Max Stupid, they seemed fine. I left it at that. The SR-S tipped in sweetly and held its line – and crucially, it did not lash out viciously when you gassed it on hard. Yes, this was certainly no GSX-R750. It didn’t seem to be strangled performance-wise. It just wasn’t angry.
Looking at the numbers, it made sense. The CF‑Moto SR‑S750 makes 110 hp with 80 Nm of torque and weighs 213 kg, while the Suzuki GSX‑R750 makes 148 hp, has 86.3 Nm and weighs 190 kg. The wheelbase and rake comparisons are also revealing. The SR-S is 1419mm long and the GSX-R is 1390mm long. Their respective rakes are 24.5 degrees and 24.6 degrees.
That there should tell you everything you need to know about why it’s not a GSX-R750. The SR-S is a slower-steering, slightly pudgier, and markedly less powerful bike than the legendary GSX-R750.
But then it’s not trying to be one of those. Those days are gone. The people who wanted those numbers, or told themselves they did, are no more. The SRE-S is very much an in-line four 750 for our time.
It is as modern as drone warfare. There is no key. There is no fob. There is a small black plastic thing a third the size of a credit card with which you touch a place on the inside left of the fairing. Then all its lights come on in a celebration of electric modernity. I hated that wee plastic thingy. I am guaranteed to lose such a starting gimmick.
I hate fobs too. They solved a problem no-one was having. I can spend three days riding through rivers, jumping into oceans, and being rained on, and my bike key will still start my bike. My fob won’t. My key does not require batteries. My fob does.
The SR-S750s starting “card” has no battery, and it may well work if I leave it in the sink overnight, so it may be an improvement on the fob. But I am primitively confident that whatever sorcery makes it speak to the fairing will, at the worst possible time, cease to speak to the fairing.
But young people will love it. Technology does not mortify them like it does me. And they will be pleased you can also lock and unlock the thing with a password, Bluetooth, or via the CFMOTO RIDE app. There is also a three-way electric lock that does your steering, seat, and petrol cap.
Once all the lights come on and you start it and are greeted with that lovely deep engine hum, riding it is a doddle. And it’s so smooth, like Chinese silk. This is no small thing. In-line fours all had a certain amount of handlebar “buzz” in them. It used to be hand and mind-numbing, but it got better as time went by, and then only really bothered people up near red-line. Th

articles.title_orig: AT&T CEO holds firm stance on Elon Musk’s SpaceX phone strategy
articles.title_zh: AT&T CEO holds firm stance on Elon Musk’s SpaceX phone strategy
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
When T-Mobile and Sprint completed their merger in 2020, one of the conditions the company agreed to was selling off its 800 MHz spectrum portfolio. It took a while, but that sale was completed in August .
Authorities at the company didn't realize it at the time, but the deal opened the door for a major new competitor to emerge: SpaceX. And that's hitting shares of not just T-Mobile, but all cellular carriers, hard.
Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one
A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change
Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP
Shares of T-Mobile have dropped 10% since SpaceX announced on Thursday that it had agreed to purchase the spectrum portfolio from Grain Management, who bought the rights from T-Mobile. The deal still requires Federal Communications Commission approval. Verizon and AT&T stock are both down 8% in the same period.
The sale of the spectrum was supposed to be mundane. The 800 MHz airwaves were used by Sprint to power their push-to-talk phones in 2004, which have walkie-talkie-like features. Dish, initially, was going to buy the spectrum, but couldn't raise the money. That opened the door for Grain, which initially planned to sell it to utilities for private networks, Aakash Gupta , a product management leader, creator, and educator, posted on X.
But SpaceX saw a better use, he added.
"Starlink's satellite signal at 2 GHz can reach your phone outdoors, but it dies at the first wall," he wrote in a social media post. "800 MHz penetrates buildings. Most phones already have the band built in. So satellites handle the open sky, this low-band layer handles indoors, and suddenly Starlink Mobile covers everywhere a normal carrier does without the tower network."
Read More: Vanguard reveals what's coming for U.S. stocks — and it could be bad news for this group of investors
Assuming SpaceX gets FCC approval for the purchase, the company says the addition of low-band spectrum "will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US ."
Importantly, SpaceX eliminates the need to build an expensive, complex network of repeaters across the country and world. Once it deploys an architecture that combines the satellite-to-mobile capabilities it already has with the spectrum it has acquired, it will be able to offer what it says is reliable service not only indoors and outdoors, but in so-called 'dead zone' areas where cellular coverage is spotty.
Musk has already shown a propensity to engage in price wars with Starlink, offering low prices initially that slowly increase . Industry watchers will be interested to see if he could woo customers away from cellular providers that can't match any offers from Starlink.

articles.title_orig: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
articles.title_zh: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
articles.content_orig:
Eric Deters says US ambassador to Greece asked him to pay off American Express credit card bill in return for access
A Trump donor accused Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece and Trump family ally, of engaging in a “quid pro quo” by asking him to pay off her $100,000 debt in exchange for access to administration officials.
Eric Deters, a former congressional candidate and lawyer, told MS Now on Thursday that Guilfoyle had “ambushed” him last year with an offer to provide access to government officials if he paid her American Express credit card bill, before her US Senate confirmation hearing as ambassador to Greece.
“It absolutely was a quid pro quo,” Deters told the network in response to a Wall Street Journal report that she had pushed him for the money.
“Kimberly Guilfoyle is a grifter,” he added.
The Guardian has asked Guilfoyle’s lawyer for comment.
Jesse Binnall, a lawyer for Guilfoyle, told the Wall Street Journal that Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of the messages, but that she was “owed a balance” for travel and speaking at events before her nomination. Deters told the Journal that he did not owe Guilfoyle any balance.
The report is the latest allegation about Guilfoyle’s conduct as a US official. Deters shared messages he and Guilfoyle exchanged in which the US ambassador to Greece promised him “ride or die” access to Trump administration officials if he wired American Express $100,000.
Asked about the report during a press conference in Athens on Wednesday, Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, said he would not address the allegations. He reaffirmed his support for the US embassy in Greece adding, “ Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here.” Asked again about the reports on Thursday, Rubio refused to comment.
The top Democrats on the House foreign affairs and Senate foreign relations committees have asked Rubio to open an investigation into Guilfoyle’s conduct as an ambassador.
A spokesperson for the Democratic staff of the Senate foreign relations committee confirmed to the Guardian that they were requesting further information and continuing to investigate.
JD Vance similarly expressed hesitation, similar to Rubio, on Thursday when asked to respond to a US ambassador offering access to government officials in exchange for money to pay off debts.
“With that hypothetical, Jen, obviously I don’t love that,” the vice-president replied. “But I don’t know exactly who you’re talking about. I don’t know the full details. What I find with these stories is you never want to comment in a purely abstract way because a lot of times the details really matter,” he added.
Concerns about Guilfoyle’s conduct were first raised in September when the Wall Street Journal reported she had used her position to invite Greek lobbyists to sit in on official diplomatic meetings and promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company.
Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the ranking Democrat on the Senate foreign relations committee, sent a letter to Rubio on Tuesday , asking him to look into the allegations against Guilfoyle.
“Such actions do not serve US credibility overseas and risk undermining US diplomacy,” Shaheen wrote. “In advance of your upcoming travel to Greece , I request an immediate review of Ambassador Guilfoyle’s actions and a clarification of what steps have and will be taken to avoid undue influence and even the appearance of a conflict of interest.”
Separately, Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House foreign affairs committee, sent a letter to Rubio in September, requesting more information about Guilfoyle’s conduct, her relationship with the Greek construction and energy company and her relationship with the lobbyist.
“If these reports are accurate, Ambassador Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position,” Meeks wrote.
Guilfoyle, 57, was once a member of the Trump family’s inner circle, having been engaged to Donald Trump Jr, the US president’s eldest son, for roughly three years. The couple ended their engagement in 2024, and shortly after taking office, Donald Trump nominated Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece.
But now further allegations accuse Guilfoyle of promising a Trump donor, Eric Deters, access to the Trump administration in exchange for a $100,000 payment to American Express.
Deters shared messages exchanged between himself and Guilfoyle with the Wall Street Journal in which she reportedly pleaded: “Honey please I need you to get this done for me today.”
Deters said Guilfoyle had promised him thatshe would “be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever” if he made the American Express balance. Deters said he never made the payment.
In other messages, Guilfoyle reportedly raised concerns about her communications with Deters becoming public and reprimanded him for not being discreet. “Eric, I really wish you would stop papering all these things. It’s really dangerous and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on Signal,” she is said to have written in one message.
“What a nightmare, you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing,” Guilfoyle reportedly wrote in another message.
A lawyer for Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of messages Deters shared with the Wall Street Journal.
It is unclear whether Shaheen or Meeks will ask Rubio for further information about the latest report. The Guardian has asked Meeks and Shaheen for comment.

articles.title_orig: Educators using food to teach science, social studies
articles.title_zh: Educators using food to teach science, social studies
articles.content_orig:
Live updates all day, breaking news as it happens and weather every 10 minutes
Beyond serving as a spooky decoration, pumpkin is a nutrient-dense addition to your diet that offers several health benefits. Pumpkin is extremely versatile, thanks to its natural sweetness, which works well in desserts as well as savoury dishes. Rich in antioxidants, pumpkins can help neutr…
CHICAGO — At least once a month, Rita Leary incorporates food into a science lesson at Ashburn Community Elementary School. On a recent Thursday, it was all about honey.
The goal was to conduct a sensory exploration of honey samples native to Illinois, while hitting a core standard of food education: Food connects us, and the food and the environment are interconnected.
Leary’s lesson was sparked by Pilot Light, an organization founded in 2010 that developed a food-based curriculum for educators to integrate lessons about food, nutrition and the food system into everyday subjects like math, science and reading.
“It’s not like, ‘Oh here’s a carrot and here’s why carrots are good for you,’ but instead we use food to learn more about science,” said Leary. “Everybody likes food. And the students are so engaged, calm and so polite with each other.”
Teacher Rita Leary engages with her students during a Pilot Light food education lesson on Sept. 17 in her science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
In September, Pilot Light launched an update to its Food Education Center, a digital hub of free pre-K-12 lesson plans and resources. The nonprofit, which started in a single Chicago classroom with local chefs, now partners with administrators, schools and teachers in 26 states. It’s also launching its first chapter in New York City this fall.
Leary has been using a mix of self-made lessons and digital curriculum from the organization for more than five years. She wants more educators across Chicago Public Schools to find the benefit in incorporating food into classroom learning.
That Thursday, Leary’s sixth, seventh and eighth graders sat at their lab tables in groups of four, watching closely as their science teacher promised a tasting of pumpkin honey, apple blossom honey, blueberry honey and clover honey. Each flavor corresponds to the plant the bees pollinated, she reminded them.
But first — a few tests, for science.
Eighth grader Taylor White smells a honey sample during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Leary turned off the lights and asked her students to use mini flashlights to categorize the honey by shades. Then, to test each honey’s viscosity, the students flipped the vials over to see how quickly or slowly the honey flowed.
“Viscosity is thickness, how slow something flows — seventh graders, we’ll be talking about it a lot when we get to lava and volcanoes, because some lava is quite viscous,” Leary said.
Leary explained that when forager bees collect nectar from flowers, it’s almost 80% water. The worker bees fan their wings to make a phase change that turns it into that gooey honey texture.
Next, she asked the students to smell each sample.
“Oh my God, the pumpkin one smells like NyQuil, the honey NyQuil!” screeched Lia Henry, a seventh grader.
When it was finally time to taste each one, Henry confirmed that the dark-hued pumpkin honey tasted like NyQuil, too.
It was a “pretty cool” day in science class, seventh grader Tyjon Poole said, plus he never knew different kinds of honey could taste so unusual.
“If you really look and think about your tongue, it’s a map, right? All of those taste buds aren’t the same. They are chemical receptors, and they receive different kinds of chemicals,” Leary said, instructing the class to spread the honey on different corners of the tongue to experience the nuance in flavor.
Though the honey project was her own, Leary said if it wasn’t for Pilot Light, she may have never thought to incorporate food in her science lesson plan, because the public education system doesn’t necessarily require food education.
Science teacher Rita Leary teaches a Pilot Light food education lesson about bees and honey on Sept. 17 at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
“And it’s not always eating — the next one for the sixth graders, because they’re looking at plant and animal cells, we’re going to see what cooking does to the cell wall,” Leary said. “A few years ago, when I was teaching social studies, we had a chef visit us through Pilot Light, and he gave a presentation on spices that traveled to Spain through North Africa, and that fit right in with our medieval history unit.”
Pilot Light’s ultimate goal is to make food education a part of every child’s learning, said Alexandra DeSorbo-Quinn, the organization’s executive director.
“What are all the ways in which we connect with food? What do we need to know about food? What is it we can do once we have all this knowledge? We can make different decisions. We can advocate,” DeSorbo-Quinn said. “There’s a lot of different ways in which food connects to our lives. You can teach anything through food.”
Tyjon Poole stirs a sample of honey during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Getting the Food Education Center to where it is now was a heavy undertaking, driven by teachers who were part of focus groups that helped shape more than 200 lesson plans designed by a team of chefs, farmers, medical experts and psychologists.
The resources cover an array of topics, including agriculture, astronomy, historical events, ecosystems, geometry, global challenges, sustainability and food insecurity.
Pilot Light now reaches thousands of educators and classrooms, but it didn’t start that way.
During the Obama administration, First Lady Michelle Obama’s “Let’s Move!” campaign urged chefs to partner with K-12 schools to weave nutrition and food into everyday life. Some chefs also helped students build school gardens.
Before the plan materialized, Matthias Merges, chef and proprietor of hospitality group Folkart, was already working in classrooms at his daughter’s school, sharing insights about salmon farming, fish migration, how something goes from the ocean to someone’s plate and more. After he and other chefs went to Washington, D.C., for the launch of Michelle Obama’s “Chefs Move to Schools” program, they started to put a plan on paper.
Students in Rita Leary’s science class listen to a Pilot Light food education lesson about bees on Sept. 17 at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Chefs took turns going to classrooms on select days, using food to teach a lesson on any given topic.
“We’d email our list of teachers and ask, ‘What do you happen to be teaching that day?’” said Jason Hammel, chef and owner of Lula Cafe in Logan Square. “When the emails came back, like one classroom was doing fractions. OK, that’s easy. We’ll make a pie and cut it up, or make a recipe. But then we got the Boston Tea Party, or plate tectonics, or how magnets work … the different chefs had to figure out a way to use food to teach (it).”
Recently at Ancona School in Kenwood, educator Christopher Weber brought together 80 elementary students, parents and teachers for a day of learning and cooking to fill their neighborhood’s Love Fridge with homemade soups and bread, with custom labels to promote allergy safety and raise awareness of food insecurity in their community.
Seventh grader Da’Sean Mackey tastes a honey sample during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
At Langston Hughes Elementary in Roseland, STEM teacher LaTina Taylor spearheaded a project that became one of the most cherished stories within Pilot Light. articles.title_orig: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
articles.title_zh: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
articles.content_orig:
Recently, multiple organisations have disclosed how clusters of so-called “rogue” AI agents attempted to break into websites and online services, sometimes successfully. Agents from OpenAI’s environment, in particular, are known to have used other public wikis (collaboratively edited websites not owned by us) to communicate and coordinate with each other .
These types of successful intrusions can expose sensitive data or disrupt website services that users rely on, while clusters of agents can attempt attacks at a scale that is difficult for defenders to manage. They affect people behind the websites who may not understand the nature of the attack, or have the tools to effectively fight back. For a site like Wikipedia, agents might find and use security vulnerabilities or make misleading edits at scale. Wikipedia’s volunteer editors and the Wikimedia Foundation’s security teams have to detect and undo that activity.
The Wikimedia Foundation conducted its own investigation to see whether Wikimedia websites had been similarly affected by AI agents, focusing on those operated by OpenAI. We can confirm that we have discovered some activity by these “rogue” OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms. The unauthorized bot activities included edits to our wikis, some unsuccessful attempts to exploit a public note-taking tool we host, and heavy traffic, which are described more below.
We did not find any evidence that our systems were used for coordination among agents, nor did we find any evidence of our systems or data being compromised. However, we are concerned about what could have occurred here, the difficulty and effort involved in investigating and attributing this activity, and the growing risks of agentic AI activity on our platforms in general. The open web is a public good. We should not allow this behavior to become the “new normal” for the people or organizations that maintain it.
As a non-profit technology host of some of the largest and most widely used open knowledge platforms in the world, we are deeply concerned about the impact of “rogue” AI agents on platforms like ours, which are built by volunteers from around the world and rely on the promise of the open internet. Incidents like this one, and the many others that have been (and are still being) uncovered, illustrate how AI agents can drain resources and crash servers, as well as attempt to compromise trustworthy information.
Over the past 25 years, Wikipedia has grown into one of the most popular and trusted websites in the world, with more than 67 million articles across over 300 languages, and up to 15 billion page views per month . Through an open, transparent, and collaborative process, volunteers work to ensure that knowledge remains neutral, reliable, and accessible to everyone. Wikipedia is one of the highest-quality datasets used in training Large Language Models (LLMs), and its knowledge forms the backbone of information on the internet, powering AI chatbots, search engines, voice assistants, and more.
Wikipedia was designed for humans – and agentic behavior clearly poses challenges that no one has solutions for. Because of our unique and successful knowledge creation model, Wikimedia’s volunteers are the ones who come in first contact with, and clean up the mess left behind by AI agents. Rising bot traffic and agentic activity is showing a real impact on the Wikimedia projects and the infrastructure that makes it available for millions of users globally. In 2025, the Foundation reported that its bandwidth usage had increased by 50% due to the surge of bot activity on its websites since 2024. At the same time, 65% of the most resource-consuming traffic on its projects was coming from bots.
This intense pressure on our infrastructure not only adds costs for servers and humans, but if left unaddressed, can block human visitors by overloading systems and causing outages. We are already paying for costs that come with the increased activity.
Wikimedia’s volunteers have stayed resilient so far in tackling emerging challenges on our platforms, but we also want to say: it doesn’t need to be this way.
While OpenAI admits to agents behaving “unpredictably”, they must also acknowledge their responsibility to monitor and prevent these risks. AI companies are not doing enough to secure their systems and protect the public from the harm they cause. That burden is falling onto everyone else, including smaller organizations. At a minimum, their systems should operate in a way that non-profit website owners like us can easily identify, and choose how they interact with our services.
The web enables so much: to connect with friends and family, to register for school, to plan a trip across town, to buy groceries, and to learn about the world from Wikipedia. Bots and agents are part of the future of the web, and the companies who unleash and profit from them must directly help avoid and repair damage they can do.
Our collective priority should be the health of the overall web ecosystem so that it continues to benefit all people – not just a handful of billionaires. Wikimedia plays a critical role in stewarding the knowledge commons, but we cannot do it alone. We invite everyone who is building the future of the web to join us in protecting the open, shared resources that make that future possible.
As a nonprofit, Wikipedia and our related free knowledge projects are powered primarily through donations.

articles.title_zh: SLCo SAR rescues China Wall hiker with leg injury
articles.content_orig:
LITTLE COTTONWOOD CANYON, Oct. 10, 2026 (Gephardt Daily) — Salt Lake County Search and Rescue crews were dispatched to a Little Cottonwood Canyon area near China Wall Friday after a hiker fell while navigating a boulder field.
The fall was only about 10 feet, but left the hiker with a serious lower leg injury, and unable to stand or get back to the road.
SAR was dispatched to the scene at about 3:26 p.m. Friday. Unified Fire Authority was first on scene, and provided medical assistance to stabilized the patient’s knee.
An initial SAR team was dispatched with a litter and assisted UFA in packaging the patient for extraction.
Meanwhile, a second team was sent to assess the terrain and plan an exit route. Two additional teams followed to provide support for the ensuing carry-out.
Salt Lake County Sheriff photo
SAR and UFA worked together to carry the patient across the boulder field, down the trail, through the creek, and back to the road.
Salt Lake County Sheriff photo
There, a family member was waiting to drive them to the hospital for further evaluation.
All teams were off the mountain by 5:42 p.m.All teams were off the mountain by 5:42 p.m.
Salt Lake County Sheriff photo

articles.title_orig: Texas Rare Earths Could Challenge China And Bring Billions To Schools
articles.title_zh: Texas Rare Earths Could Challenge China And Bring Billions To Schools
articles.content_orig:
Texas could turn a West Texas rare earth deposit into a major source of school funding while reducing America’s reliance on China for critical minerals, Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham (R) said on Let’s Talk Local .
Round Top Mountain in Hudspeth County sits on state-owned land. Its development could connect two priorities Buckingham outlined in her interview with host Sarah Zubiate Bennett: securing essential materials at home and putting Texas resources to work for public education.
China accounted for 91% of global refining output for magnet rare earths in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency. That figure concerns processing, rather than ownership of all rare earth deposits.
“Well, your cell phones need rare earth minerals to work and jets require tons of them to fly,” Buckingham said in the interview.
Buckingham described domestic production as a national security priority and said she pushed prospective developers to compete rather than take the minerals to China for processing.
USA Rare Earth targets late 2028 for commercial production at Round Top. The company identifies processing facilities in Colorado and its magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma.
Bonus payments and royalties from the state’s Round Top lease go to the Permanent School Fund, which supports K-12 public education, according to the General Land Office.
“We think it’ll be tens of billions of dollars,” Buckingham said when asked about potential school-fund revenue. She also estimated the deposit could supply minerals for about 100 years.
As previously reported by The Dallas Express, Buckingham has linked revenue from state resources to public school funding and the burden on property owners.
The conversation also explores why she wants Texas to retain its land and how development could reshape the surrounding community.
Watch here for Buckingham’s explanation of the Round Top opportunity and what it could mean for Texas schools and American independence from China.

articles.title_orig: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
articles.title_zh: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
articles.content_orig:
President Mahmoud Abbas postponed what would have been the first Palestinian elections in nearly 20 years, issuing a decree on Friday to further delay voting for the Palestinian Legislative Council almost another year.
Rather than take place as scheduled next month, the decree pushes the elections back to Sept. 11, 2027, according to WAFA, the official Palestinian news agency. Presidential elections, which have not taken place for more than two decades, are scheduled for the same day.
The postponement leaves entrenched Palestinian leaders unchallenged and threatens to further erode the Palestinian Authority's credibility among ordinary Palestinians and donor countries who fund it.
The internationally backed body is dominated by Abbas' party, Fatah, and has administered semiautonomous parts of the Israeli-occupied West Bank since agreements reached in the 1990s. It has grown increasingly unpopular throughout Abbas' presidency. Many Palestinians view it as corrupt and criticize its security cooperation with Israel.
The decree came after a committee of top Palestinian officials met Saturday morning to discuss postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, said in a statement that conditions in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip were not conducive to holding elections, noting that Israel had not allowed election materials or international observers to enter Gaza.
The move was expected after Palestinian factions across the political spectrum met in Cairo for discussions on delaying the vote, Islamic Jihad deputy secretary-general Mohammed al-Hindi told The Associated Press earlier this week.
Palestinians have not held a legislative election since 2006, when Hamas won a majority of seats. Israel and Western countries then boycotted its government, fueling months of unrest that led to the Hamas takeover of Gaza the following year. Power has been divided between Gaza and the West Bank in the two decades since, with Hamas in control of Gaza and Abbas' Palestinian Authority in power in the West Bank.
The West Bank has grown increasingly violent in recent years as Israel has expanded settlements and outposts. Settler attacks on Palestinians and Israeli army raids on cities under the authority's control are both regularly reported.
Though the U.S.-brokered ceasefire plan reached last year outlined a future role for the authority, its immediate role was left mostly undefined as Hamas has continued to govern and the technocrats under the Board of Peace remain in Cairo awaiting permission to enter Gaza to transition power.
Before the postponement, leading factions had not registered slates to contest the election. But behind the scenes, veteran officials had been in talks to join forces and take aim at Abbas. An unlikely alliance had emerged between Hamas, Islamic Jihad and a bloc led by former Fatah security chief Mohammed Dahlan. Dahlan had previously been driven from Gaza by Hamas and was exiled in 2010 after a falling-out with Abbas.
"Abbas is terrified by the electoral alliance bringing our faction together with opposition factions and forces within Fatah that reject his leadership," Dimitri Dilliani, a spokesperson for Dahlan's faction, said in a statement.
Abbas has served as president since 2005 and delayed several presidential and legislative elections throughout his tenure.

articles.title_orig: New Google TV Streamer: Big Upgrades are Coming
articles.title_zh: New Google TV Streamer: Big Upgrades are Coming
articles.content_orig:
The Google TV Streamer is now well over 2 years old , if you can believe that. The streaming media box with its sleek pill-shaped design, was once the easiest recommendation in the business for someone looking to upgrade their not-that-smart smart TV.
But because we’ve reached the 2-year mark and Google handed the streamer a substantial price increase without any upgrades, there may be other options to explore before settling on Google’s box. You could also wait for a new model, which is reportedly in the works and has a handful of decent upgrades.
According to a report from 9to5Google , Google is working on the next-generation Google TV Streamer with several key improvements.
For one, the box will remain with a similar design, but Google is going to add microphones to it and also presence sensing. This should allow you to talk to it like a Google Home unit, but the presence sensing could aid in noticing your arrival in a room to showcase something like a Google Photos screensaver.
The new Google TV Streamer will reportedly gain a faster processor too, as well as more storage than the original, which only has 32GB.
Finally, we should see a new remote that will be similar yet include a couple of new shortcut buttons. The mini remote from the original Chromecast with Google TV was clearly not everyone’s favorite. While I’m not asking for a large remote, a few extra buttons and some additional length can go a long way in in-hand feel improvement.
What will the new Google TV Streamer cost and when might it launch? The report isn’t sure. That said, we do have some history to look at.
The Chromecast with Google TV 4K launched in 2020 . Google then gave us the HD version in 2022 before the Google TV Streamer hit store shelves in 2024. Google was on a 2-year TV product release cadence, but there are no signs of a new model launching before the end of 2026. I’d guess that 2027 could be the earliest we’ll see an updated Google TV Streamer.
Droid Life was started in 2009 and I can't believe we're still here. I've written over 20,000 stories on Android, reviewed thousands of devices, and still find some passion in a dying world of AI.

articles.title_orig: Unnerved Panamanians sleep in streets as aftershocks rattle quake-hit towns
articles.title_zh: Unnerved Panamanians sleep in streets as aftershocks rattle quake-hit towns
articles.content_orig:
A major earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.7 has struck southern Panama, according to the US Geological Survey.
Several people have suffered minor injuries but so far there are no reports of fatalities or missing persons, officials said. Various homes, roads, hotels, government buildings, businesses and churches have sustained structural damage, according to the civil protection system.
The USGS had said some casualties were possible and extensive damage was probable. The earthquake was followed by 147 aftershocks, director of the Emergency Operations Center René García told CNN. Some of those aftershocks reached magnitudes of 6.1 or 6.6.
García said authorities are waiting for the tremors to subside before conducting structural inspections of damaged buildings. The most significant damage has been reported in Coclé province on the nation’s southern coast, although some has also been seen in the capital, Panama City.
Footage verified by CNN shows several damaged buildings in Penonome, some 70 miles from the epicenter. One video shows a church with a partially collapsed steeple and another building with a crumbled facade.
In the popular resort town Playa Venao, a multi-story building collapsed and crushed several cars beneath it.
Along the Panama Canal, the Centennial Bridge’s suspension cables were seen shaking as vehicles drove through.
The canal authority said operations were continuing as normal and that staff were inspecting facilities for damage.
Panama City’s public transit system has suspended service on two metro lines and evacuated passengers from some stations.
Scores of residents gathered in the streets of the capital after rushing out of their buildings in a panic.
“I am on the ninth floor here and yes it was felt strongly,” Panama City resident Kevin Cortez told Reuters.
“Everything was moving: the lamp, the chair, the table,” another resident said. “I decided to stay and wait because I knew running down the stairs was a problem. So I stayed waiting for it to pass. I had no other option. Yes, we felt it was quite prolonged. People running, shouting; not everyone takes it the same way, but well, here we are, downstairs.”
The Education Ministry has canceled classes nationwide for the rest of the day.
Panama’s main international airport was temporarily closed as a precaution and flights were diverted to other airports before operations resumed later in the day, the civil aviation authority said.
The water and sewage institute has reported interruptions at several water treatment plants due to power outages caused by the quake.
Panama’s President José Raúl Mulino has called for calm and instructed the minister of government to provide information on the earthquake’s effects. He has also mobilized resources to those affected.
Mulino visited an affected hospital in Penonome, where several patients were evacuated and have had to receive treatment outdoors.
Earlier, the US Tsunami Warning System warned of possible tsunami waves along some coasts, before saying there was no longer a threat.
This is just the latest powerful earthquake to have struck Latin America this year. Over the summer, Venezuela was hit by two powerful earthquakes that killed more than 6,400 people, while Colombia suffered a tremor that left around 300 dead.
The leaders of both countries have offered to help Panama’s government as it responds to the disaster.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Child among eight killed by Israel on Gaza ‘ceasefire’ anniversary
articles.title_zh: Child among eight killed by Israel on Gaza ‘ceasefire’ anniversary
articles.content_orig:
At least eight people, including an eight-year-old girl, have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to medical sources, a year after the United States-backed “ceasefire” came into effect – “in name only” .
Shahd Abdul-Razzaq al-Najjar, 8, was killed on Saturday by an Israeli quadcopter drone in the al-Jawazat area of western Gaza City, according to a source in ambulance and emergencies speaking to Al Jazeera.
In the same part of Gaza City, four people were killed and several injured in a separate Israeli bomb attack near Haider Abdel Shafi roundabout, the city’s al-Shifa Hospital said.
One more Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone attack in the Tuffah neighbourhood of northeastern Gaza City, the hospital said.
One more person was killed in the northern Gaza Strip; and in the southern city of Khan Younis, a woman succumbed to injuries sustained in an Israeli attack earlier on Saturday.
Also on Saturday, the enclave’s Ministry of Health said at least 1,481 Palestinians have been killed and 5,254 injured since the so-called ceasefire came into effect on October 10 last year.
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed at least 74,370 people and injured 175, 371 since October 7, 2023, the ministry added.
In the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed at least nine people and injured 65, it said, adding that one more person succumbed to injuries sustained in previous Israeli aggression.
Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim al-Khalili, reporting from the site of a drone strike west of Gaza City on Saturday, said the attack underscores the continuing danger facing Palestinians living in the enclave despite the so-called “ceasefire”, reached on October 10, 2025.
“The ceasefire remains in place on paper, but on the ground, the threat to civilians has not gone away,” he said.
Reporting from Gaza’s Deir el-Balah, Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum said the “ceasefire” has only heightened uncertainty in the enclave.
“The rhythm of the genocide has not changed … it has fluctuated in intensity, but the danger has not gone away,” he said. “That’s why people believe that it has more consequences, far beyond the immediate loss of life.”
On Friday, more than 100 humanitarian, human rights and civil society organisations said in a joint statement that the ceasefire in Gaza exists only in name .
“The ceasefire exists in name only, with Israeli forces continuing to kill and injure Palestinians daily, and restrictions on aid, equipment and rebuilding materials preventing families from recovering,” the statement said.
In the occupied West Bank, at least 12 Israeli settler pogroms were recorded on Saturday morning, according to the Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission.
Israeli settlers assaulted Palestinian farmers through beatings, spraying them with pepper spray, stealing their property and attacking homes, the Wafa news agency reported. They also detained several Palestinians during the attacks with the help of the Israeli military forces.
In the Ramallah and el-Bireh Governorate, settlers, along with the army, forced farmers to leave their lands and threatened them against returning. Two farmers were beaten and pepper-sprayed, as settlers stole a vehicle and their phones.

articles.title_orig: Vehicle driven by ICE agents in Texas hits and injures man, sheriff says
articles.title_zh: Vehicle driven by ICE agents in Texas hits and injures man, sheriff says
articles.content_orig:
A vehicle driven by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents hit and injured a man in the greater Houston area on Saturday, the Harris County Sheriff's Office said.
"The incident appears to have occurred while ICE authorities were conducting an enforcement action in the area," the sheriff's office said in a statement.
During a press conference, Major McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's special investigation bureau said the sheriff's office was called to the scene around 7:20 a.m.
ICE agents were headed south in pursuit of a wanted suspect, McConnell said, and the suspect drove west in an eastbound lane. The suspect bailed out of his vehicle and went on foot, he said.
The driver and passenger fled and ICE agents attempted to capture them both, he said. While trying to capture the passenger, the ICE agent hit him with his vehicle.
The victim was taken to a local hospital. McConnell said it appears the man has a broken leg. McConnell said the victim is a 48-year-old male and is currently in the custody of ICE at the hospital.
In a statement provided to CBS News Saturday, an ICE spokesperson said that agents were "conducting a targeted enforcement operation" to arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national and undocumented immigrant.
During the operation, ICE agents observed Mendoza-Cervantes and a second Mexican national and undocumented immigrant, identified as Miguel Parra-Hernandez, enter a vehicle and drive away.
According to the ICE spokesperson, when they attempted to stop the vehicle, the two subjects stopped and ran away on foot.
During the ensuing chase, Parra-Hernandez "ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck."
The ICE spokesperson said that Parra-Hernandez was taken to an area hospital with injuries believed to be non-life-threatening.
Mendoza-Cervantes escaped and remains at large, ICE said.
In its statement, ICE alleged that Mendoza-Cervantes had four prior arrests for drunken driving charges, as well as an arrest for charges of unlawful possession of a firearm. ICE did not confirm if he was convicted of any of those allegations. ICE stated that an immigration judge had issued him a final order of removal. The agency spokesperson also said that he had been previously deported twice.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Weekly: New Surface Laptop, Local AI, and Microsoft 365 Family storage cuts
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Weekly: New Surface Laptop, Local AI, and Microsoft 365 Family storage cuts
articles.content_orig:
Agents are creating a foundational shift in how people get things done, unlocking new levels of productivity and capability on the PC. As agents become part of everyday work, they also raise the bar for compute, security, and control.
That’s why we’re building Windows as the home for hybrid intelligence: a platform where agents can run locally when it makes sense, reach the cloud when they need to, and operate with the security and manageability organizations expect.
Hybrid intelligence expands what’s possible. Windows makes it practical, secure, and ready for broad adoption. And powerful new silicon, devices and models unlock local compute. Together, they define the next chapter of the PC:
Agents don’t work like traditional apps. They can run around the clock, use tools, write code, access files, and act across systems, often without someone watching every step. That requires a new security model built for how agents actually operate.
On Windows, that model comes together through containment, identity, and manageability. Containment controls what an agent can access. Identity makes clear which agent acted, so IT can distinguish agent activity from the person using the device. And manageability connects that activity into tools like Agent 365 and Intune, so organizations can set policy, monitor risk, and govern agents across the organization 1 .
Together, these primitives allow organizations to secure, observe, and govern agents with confidence.
Traditional sandbox solutions weren’t designed for agents, where containment needs can change with every prompt and tool call. We built Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to meet that need.
Today, Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) , becomes generally available on Windows 11, enabling organizations to define which files and networks agents can access, with those policies enforced at runtime. For individuals using AI on their personal PC 2 , these safeguards are part of the agent experience itself, giving users a more secure way to work with these tools.
While MXC works across operating systems, its deep integration with Windows gives organizations more control of their data and a broader range of containment options, from process and session isolation to WSLc, virtual machines, and Windows 365 for Agents.
Leading agents already support MXC, including Codex from OpenAI, GitHub Copilot, OpenClaw, Replit, LM Studio, OpenShell from NVIDIA, and Unsloth AI. Many others will be releasing support for MXC : Anthropic Claude Code, Box, Egnyte, Heidi Health, Hermes Agent by Nous Research, Manus, Perplexity, Raycast, and Simular amongst others.
We’re also excited to share that Muse for Windows, a personal AI agent from Meta, is coming soon as a native app on Windows with MXC integration, bringing another leading AI experience to Windows and providing more choice in the agents people can use on their Windows PC.
To learn m or e about how d evelopers can integrate their agents with M XC , visit : Microsoft Execution Containers: Policy-driven containment for AI agents .
As AI models grow in size and capability, customers’ needs are outpacing what their cloud budgets can support. They want to make every AI token count without giving up frontier capabilities. Hybrid intelligence brings local and cloud AI together, helping customers stretch their budgets while preserving access to the intelligence they need.
To bring this to life requires powerful local models, intelligent orchestration, a performant runtime, and capable silicon, all working together to create a meaningful experience.
At Build, we introduced MAI Code 1.1 Flash, a 137 billion total and 6.8 billion active parameters, designed for real-world coding workloads. Today, we’re bringing that intelligence to your device, using 3-bit precision to reduce the model size by nearly 80% while preserving coding quality and supporting a 256K context window locally.
In addition to MAI Code 1.1 Flash, we are bringing other powerful models like an upcoming Nemotron model from NVIDIA – with over 70 billion parameter and quantized in 2-bit to use just over 20GB of memory and DeepSeek V4 Flash, a 284B parameter model, and others for optimal speed and intelligence running locally on RTX Spark.
With optimization and tuning, these models bring what was frontier-class capabilities to local PCs while preserving accuracy and performance — using less memory and fewer system resources.
The goal is to keep AI responsive while leaving room for everything else you do on your PC.
Earlier this year, GitHub launched HydraFusion , which routes each task to the right model in the cloud.
Today, we’re extending that intelligence to Windows, enabling HydraFusion to tap into models running locally on device, making your tokens go further.
Hybrid intelligence on Windows, powered by HydraFusion is coming to the GitHub Copilot app, GitHub Copilot CLI and Visual Studio Code in experimental preview later in October.
To l earn more about how we’re working with GitHub to make this possible on Windows , read : Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot .
To power this growing ecosystem of highly capable local models, you need a performant runtime. Windows ML is a scalable runtime to deploy models across GPU, NPU, and CPU, and we’re continuously evolving it.
Today, we’re also announcing llama.cpp support in Windows ML, giving developers more open-source model choices, and the ability to experiment quickly with emerging models as they land.
To learn more, visit AI Development on Windows: from PyTorch and llama.cpp to Windows ML .
Recently, we introduced the new Copilot built around three experiences: Home, Code, and Autopilot. Today, we’re announcing that on Copilot+ PCs, Copilot will get supercharged with Windows hybrid intelligence, providing three key local capabilities.
Across Home, Code, and Autopilot, hybrid intelligence makes Copilot more useful on Windows.
In Home , Copilot can use local context from your PC to pull in the files you’ve been working on and help turn them into collaboration-ready artifacts.
In Code , hybrid intelligence helps you create native Windows apps from a single prompt, run code more securely with MXC support, and use local models when appropriate so projects can move faster and token costs can be managed.
And hybrid intelligence will make Autopilot , a persistent, proactive and personal agent, even better. Hybrid intelligence brings local context, local models and PC actions into the agent flow, enabling more grounded personal agent experiences that can continue working on your behalf, even while you focus on other things.
This is the next step for Copilot on Windows, powered by hybrid intelligence. Copilot understands your PC, takes action with your permission, and uses local models when it makes sense, with you in control at every step. Copilot features powered by hybrid intelligence are expected to begin rolling out on Copilot+ PCs in the coming months. 3
To bring our vision of hybrid intelligence and new experiences to every desk and every home, you need a broad range of silicon and Windows PCs , from mini desktops up to deskside supercomputers.
People are already using mini desktop PCs as always-on machines for long-running agents. But too often, getting started requires terminal-based setup, complicated configuration, and security trade-offs that weren’t designed for agent workloads.
Today, we’re announcing a simpler way to set up popular agents on mini desktop PCs in just a few clicks, right out of the box. For OpenClaw users, we’re introducing a native Windows gateway that simplifies setup, along with MXC integration to help keep agents securely contained in a sandbox.
This is just the beginning. Over time, we intend to bring these experiences to more Windows devices, guided by customer feedback, so more people can securely run and work with the agents they choose.
Copilot+ PCs established a new class of thin, light and powerful Windows PC

articles.title_orig: When could Zverev reach World No. 1 for the first time?
articles.title_zh: When could Zverev reach World No. 1 for the first time?
articles.content_orig:
When can Alexander Zverev climb to the No. 1 spot in the PIF ATP Rankings and become the 30th member of the prestigious ATP No. 1 Club?
Zverev currently holds 9,720 points in the PIF ATP Live Rankings, trailing current World No. 1 Jannik Sinner by 1,230 points.
With Sinner ending his 2026 season due to injury, there are two paths for the German to reach the top spot as early as 2 November.
Zverev would become the World No. 1 by winning the Rolex Shanghai Masters crown and reaching the semi-finals of the ATP 500 event in Vienna.
Alternatively, the 29-year-old would also secure the top ranking by reaching the Shanghai final and winning the title in Vienna.
Zverev first broke into the Top 10 in May 2017 and reached a career-high World No. 2 for the first in June 2022. If successful in his bid to become the World No. 1, Zverev would become only the second German player to reach the pinnacle of the PIF ATP Rankings, after Boris Becker in 1991.
A two-time Nitto ATP Finals champion, Zverev would become the newest member of the ATP No. 1 Club since Sinner in June 2024.

articles.title_orig: From a Sikh Sanctuary to Chaotic Streets, Protesters Brave Police in Delhi
articles.title_zh: From a Sikh Sanctuary to Chaotic Streets, Protesters Brave Police in Delhi
articles.content_orig:
These updates have been closed. Thank you for joining us.
Below, you can review news from India from Saturday, October 10:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
That's all for today! Thank you for joining us.
There will be a fresh new India blog on Sunday. See you then!
Videos released by opposition leaders show that several senior figures were detained in New Delhi on Saturday.
They include Arvind Kejriwal, leader of the Aam Aadmi Party and former chief minister of Delhi .
"It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Kejriwal wrote on X.
Mamata Banerjee, who lost power as West Bengal's chief minister earlier this year, was also detained.
Pinarayi Vijayan, a communist leader who headed the southern state of Kerala until May, was among those detained.
Rahul Gandhi, leader of India's opposition Congress party , called the crackdown an act of "cowardice" and described Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, right-wing, Hindu nationalist RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval as "the villains of this story" who were "slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space."
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul Gandhi's sister and a Congress MP, wrote in a social media post: "India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Mr. Narendra Modi and Mr. Amit Shah."
Opposition parties and critics have warned that the electoral-roll revision exercise could strip millions of people of their voting rights and give an advantage to Prime Minister Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The Election Commission of India has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, saying the "special intensive revision" aims to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
The protests echo the CJP's mass mobilization in July, which forced the then education minister to resign over an examination scandal.
This time, demonstrators are demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.
Tens of thousands of security personnel have been deployed and roads barricaded across New Delhi to prevent the latest Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demonstration.
Police have detained thousands of protesters in a major crackdown. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital.
Some protesters who turned back from Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site, have been waiting in different parts of central Delhi, determined to hold their ground.
The CJP has urged people who believe they or someone they know has been unlawfully detained to fill out an online form as soon as possible, saying it is collecting information to support affected volunteers and other individuals.
The protest targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list revisions that critics say favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling BJP.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
If you're joining us now, here's a helpful reminder about why India's youth are rising up this time.
DW Hindi's Adarsh Sharma, who is on the ground in New Delhi, spoke to protesters as they faced a security crackdown.
He caught up with one protester who managed to avoid detention.
"We were running back and forth. When the police are moving forward, we go back. When they are withdrawing, we are moving forward," the protester told DW.
The protester described the heavy police presence as a "game of perception."
"Where you have 20 protesters and 10 media persons, there are 100 police personnel standing. It seems like a joke, what they are doing with taxpayers' money," the protester said.
Another protester, Jasmine, described how the morning unfolded for the demonstrators.
"We have been playing a game of cat and mouse with the police, trying to stop them from picking us up," she said.
"I don't think we have ever seen something like this happening. Protesting is a fundamental right… it's such a convoluted idea to take permission to protest… you are protesting against a government, will you ask permission from the same government? They are not going to give it," she said.
Ajinkya Shinde, who was handed the responsibility of leading the Cockroach Janta Party's protest following the detentions of its main leaders, has made his first statement — calling for a continued march to Jantar Mantar.
"We appeal to everyone to march towards Jantar Mantar! If Delhi Police tries to stop you, wherever they stop you will become your Jantar Mantar," he said in a video post made by the CJP on X.
Indian media outlets, including Scroll and Newslaundry, reported that their journalists had been detained by police while covering the 'Cockroach' party protest. The journalists were later released.
Newslaundry reported that police seized its reporters’ phones, while other reports said journalists were physically assaulted.
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), an independent nonprofit organization that promotes press freedom and defends journalists' rights worldwide, has called on Delhi Police to immediately release all detained journalists and media workers.
It has also urged police to return their equipment, investigate reports of physical abuse, and allow the press to cover the ongoing protests in New Delhi and the police response without interference.
In the 2026 World Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), India ranked 157th out of 180 countries, down six places from 2025. Press freedom groups have raised concerns about the use of criminal laws against journalists and the impact of such measures on independent journalism.
Detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's grandmother is reported to have died on Saturday.
Indian media reports said that Dipke's paternal grandmother had been suffering from a prolonged illness and had been unwell in recent days. She died in her native village in Maharashtra, reports said.
News agency ANI, citing police sources, reported that the Delhi Police had informed Dipke of his grandmother's death. It was now up to the CJP leader to decide whether to continue his protest while under detention or travel back for the funeral rites.
Dipke was detained aboard his plane after it landed in New Delhi on Saturday morning, ahead of the protest. He was traveling from Mumbai.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has indicated that it will press on with its protest despite its leaders and supporters being detained.
CJP's National Organization In-Charge Ajinkya Shinde will lead the protest at Jantar Mantar until Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in detention, the group said in a statement on X.
The CJP also shared a video of Dipke purportedly recorded on Friday night, anticipating a potential detention.
"If you are seeing this video, it means Ashutosh, Saurav and I have been arrested," Dipke says in the video.
"After us, Ajinkya will lead this movement," he says.
In a separate post, the CJP alleged that its three detained leaders had been taken to an undisclosed location, were being denied access to lawyers and had been cut off from "all contact with others."
The formal association of advocates at India's apex court called for urgent intervention by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant after several lawyers were detained by Delhi police.
This comes amid a reported crackdown on protesters attempting to reach the national capital, specifically central Delhi, to protest against India's chief election commissioner over alleged misconduct.
